records.title: Mechanistically distinct classes of BCR::ABL1 mutations confer resistance to asciminib
records.abstract: The first-in-class allosteric BCR::ABL1 inhibitor asciminib has expanded the therapeutic landscape of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying secondary resistance remain incompletely understood. We investigated clinically observed asciminib resistance mutations by integrating structural modeling, hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), quantitative biochemical assays and molecular dynamics simulations. Resistance mutations were grouped into two mechanistically distinct classes: Mutations within the BCR::ABL1 myristate pocket (class I) and mutations located up to 40 Å from the asciminib binding site in the kinase N-lobe, SH2-kinase domain (KD) linker and SH3 domain (class II). HDX-MS demonstrated that asciminib induces conformational stabilization across the KD extending beyond the myristate pocket, establishing a long-range allosteric network. We show that class I mutations reduced asciminib affinity up to 90-fold, consistent with steric interference at the binding site. In contrast, class II mutations retained wildtype binding affinity despite conferring clinical resistance. Instead, the class II mutations F359I and M244V increased intrinsic kinase activity and enhanced BCR::ABL1 autophosphorylation, indicating overactivation. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed allosteric communication linking the myristate and ATP-binding pockets, which is disrupted by class II mutations. Together, these findings establish that asciminib resistance arises through two distinct mechanisms: direct impairment of drug binding or disruption of the asciminib binding-induced autoinhibited conformation. Our study provides a mechanistic framework for understanding resistance to allosteric BCR::ABL1 inhibitors and has important implications for resistance monitoring, combination therapies and therapeutic sequencing.

records.title: Upfront whole genome and transcriptome sequencing to improve diagnosis in inherited bone marrow failure syndromes
records.abstract: Inherited bone marrow failure syndromes (IBMFS) are monogenic disorders characterized by single or multilineage cytopenias from hypoproliferative dyshematopoiesis. Diagnosis is challenging because of substantial clinical and pathological overlap between individual IBMFS entities and acquired diseases such as immune aplastic anemia. Conventional genetic testing using targeted panels or whole exome sequencing incompletely captures the spectrum of pathogenic variation, leaving a substantial proportion of cases undiagnosed. We evaluated the utility of upfront whole genome and transcriptome sequencing (WGTS) in 237 patients with suspected IBMFS using non-hematopoietic DNA. Median age was 29 years (range 3 months-76 years) and 34.6% were under 18 years. Clinically-accredited sequencing was performed with real-time return of results to guide patient management and familial testing. A molecular diagnosis was established in 87/237 patients (36.7%), spanning hereditary thrombocytopenia, telomere biology disorders, Diamond-Blackfan anemia, severe congenital neutropenia, Shwachman-Diamond syndrome, Fanconi anemia and other IBMFS. A further four patients were diagnosed with non-hematological genetic conditions and seven patients with secondary actionable findings. Novel pathogenic mechanisms including retrotransposon-mediated gene disruption were identified. Further, novel associations with primary IBMFS-like presentations (THRA) as well as definitive evidence of gene-disease associations (MEIS1, TUBB) were established. Acceptability of WGTS based on the established Theoretical Framework of Acceptability was high among patients and carers. Upfront WGTS in suspected IBMFS provides a high diagnostic yield when compared with other genomic approaches, identifies actionable genomic abnormalities, and expands the spectrum of disease mechanisms and gene associations in IBMFS.

records.title: Multimodal omics identifies a lymphoid-biased multipotent progenitor population with limited age-associated remodeling
records.abstract: Hematopoietic aging is marked by declining regenerative capacity and a shift from lymphoid to myeloid output. Previous studies have focused primarily on hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), yet whether aging uniformly remodels the hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) compartment, or selectively affects distinct populations, remains largely unknown. To address this, we profile HSCs and multipotent progenitors MPP1-6 from young and aged mice across transcriptomic, epigenomic, metabolomic and lipidomic layers, together with single-cell division and in vivo serial transplantation assays. We identify young MPP6 (negative for CD150, CD34, CD48 and CD135) as an HSC-like, lymphoid-biased population with long-term reconstitution capacity, positioned within the top-tier of the differentiation hierarchy and marked by low global chromatin accessibility and metabolic activity. Upon aging, MPP6 preserved long-term lymphoid reconstitution, underwent limited transcriptional and regulatory remodeling, and did not accumulate polyunsaturated phospholipids or show mitochondrial oxidation. By contrast, most HSPCs, and particularly HSCs, underwent pronounced age-associated changes, including myeloid-biased expansion, metabolic rewiring, extensive distal regulatory alteration and accumulation of long-chain polyunsaturated phospholipids linked to increased oxidative stress. Pseudotime analysis further resolved the aged MPP6 compartment into two subsets, including a dormant, lymphoid-biased Dlk1-expressing population characterized by reduced mitochondrial activity, which was distinctly affected by inflammatory challenge in vivo. Together, these findings establish MPP6 as a comparatively resilient population within the aged HSPC compartment and suggest that it may represent a potential target for restoring hematopoietic balance.

records.title: The Pathogen Recognition Receptor RIG-I is Functional in Platelets and Limits Thrombotic Responses
records.abstract: Influenza is associated with increased thrombotic risk, and its viral RNA (vRNA) can be sensed by pattern-recognition receptor RIG-I, but the function of RIG-I in platelets remains unknown. We sought to determine whether RIG-I can signal in platelets and contribute to thrombotic outcomes. Using RT-qPCR, SDS-PAGE, NATIVE-PAGE, and proteomic methods in platelets from non-infected and influenza-infected patients, we show that RIG-I is present and functional. Platelet-RIG-I activation by influenza-derived-vRNA did not result in uniform α- or δ-granule release, or to interferon-pathway activation. Instead, RIG-I signaled through MAVS to increase MLKL-phosphorylation (pMLKL), oligomerization, and S100A10 (but not S100A8/A9) release and surface presence. Oligomerized pMLKL led to surface punctures, evident by scanning electron microscopy, which were visible in both platelets and thrombin-induced platelet clots. Consistent with S100A10 surface localization, RIG-I activation in presence of plasminogen reduced platelet aggregation and led to increased disaggregation in presence of urokinase-type plasminogen activator. Disruption of RIG-I/MAVS signaling through MAVS deficiency was associated with increased thrombotic burden and shorter FeCl₃-induced carotid artery occlusion times during influenza infection in vivo. Consistent changes in occlusion burden were observed in the pulmonary veins of infected mice, where occluded area inversely correlated with leukocyte presence in the lung non-vascular tissue early in infection, followed by a positive association at later time points. Our study is the first to demonstrate that platelets have a functionally active vRNA-sensing RIG-I receptor that finely tunes thrombotic risk and facilitates appropriate leukocyte transmigration during infection, through non-classical platelet activation.

records.title: Terminal differentiation program of CD8 T cells guides immunotherapeutic options for CLL patients
records.abstract: Abstract Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) remains incurable and autologous T-cell-based therapies induce durable remissions in only a minority of patients. Although poor T-cell performance in CLL has been attributed to exhaustion, T cells from CLL patients retain cytokine production and lack key transcriptional markers of exhaustion, suggesting an alternative state of differentiation. Here, we performed an integrated phenotypic, epigenetic and functional analysis of circulating CD8⁺ T cells from treatment-naive CLL patients to define the nature and therapeutic relevance of terminal differentiation in CLL. CD8⁺ T cells from treatment-naive CLL patients were enriched for a terminally differentiated, CD27⁻CD28⁻CD57⁺KLRG1⁺ population with several senescence-associated features, including increased cell size, granularity, β-galactosidase activity, and reduced basal autophagy. However, these cells lacked key hallmarks of irreversible senescence. Instead, CLL T cells mounted robust but transient proliferative bursts and developed activation-associated γH2AX signals followed by impaired persistence and increased cell death upon repeated activation. Especially CD57⁺ T cells were vulnerable and incompatible with the experimental steps required for CAR T-cell manufacturing. The potent, acute effector function of these cells could, however, be harnessed by bispecific T-cell engagers, which induced effective cytolysis of both cell lines and primary CLL targets by these T cells. Collectively, our data support a model in which CD8+ T-cell dysfunction in CLL reflects accumulation of short-lived, terminally differentiated effector cells rather than canonical exhaustion or irreversible senescence. This state limits durable persistence required for CAR T-cell approached while preserving acute cytotoxicity relevant for bispecific antibody-based therapies in CLL.

records.title: Detection, Monitoring, and Discrimination of Amyloidogenic vs Innocent Light Chains in Systemic Amyloidoses
records.abstract: Immunoglobulin light chains (LCs) span the spectrum of B-cell clonal disorders from monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance to multiple myeloma and Waldenström macroglobulinemia. Beyond serving as disease markers, monoclonal immunoglobulins can cause organ damage in monoclonal gammopathies of clinical significance (MGCS). In AL amyloidosis the pathogenic agent is a monoclonal light chain (LC). AL amyloidosis is a treatable yet rapidly progressive condition in which early diagnosis is critical for organ preservation and survival. High-sensitivity laboratory tools for detection of amyloidogenic LCs are essential in diagnosis, while precise quantitative methods are required for monitoring treatment response and for identifying relapse, where standardized relapse definitions remain an unmet need. With increasingly effective therapies, deep hematologic response assessment and measurable residual disease detection-through mass spectrometry-based methods, flow cytometry, and next-generation sequencing-are central to decision-making. Emerging strategies to discriminate "innocent" from amyloidogenic LCs will enable pre-symptomatic intervention in patients with apparently benign monoclonal gammopathies. These approaches include biomarkers of early organ damage and LC-intrinsic features that enhance amyloid propensity (N-glycosylation, preferential germline gene usage, and reduced stability). Such tools also hold promise for the differential diagnosis of non-AL amyloidoses, particularly transthyretin (ATTR) cardiac amyloidosis-the most common form in elderly males and African-American populations-who are at elevated risk of coexisting LC-producing clones. Rapid and accurate exclusion of AL amyloidosis in this setting is now a clinical imperative. This review synthesizes current laboratory approaches and future directions for LC detection and monitoring in systemic amyloidoses, highlighting their impact on hematologic practice.

records.title: Is Circulating Tumor DNA Ready for Clinical Use in Large B-cell Lymphoma?
records.abstract: Response assessment after frontline therapy for large B-cell lymphoma risk-stratifies patients into those at low risk for relapse and those with residual disease. Positron emission tomography scans form the cornerstone of the response criteria but cannot detect molecular-only disease. Circulating tumor DNA detects measurable residual disease (MRD) after therapy which is emerging as an adjunct tool for complex clinical decision-making. We discuss how MRD after therapy can be clinically implemented and additional data needed to unlock its full potential.

records.title: Nuclear Receptor Nur77 Orchestrates Hematopoietic Lineage Commitment to Avert Anemia in Diabetes
records.abstract: Anemia is a prevalent but poorly understood complication of diabetes mellitus. Here, we identify orphan nuclear receptor Nur77 as a critical suppressor of diabetic anemia. Nur77 expression was downregulated in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) from diabetic patients with anemia. In multiple diabetic mouse models, knockout of Nur77 induced anemia, a phenotype recapitulated by bone marrow transplantation. Mechanistically, Nur77 functioned as a transcriptional repressor in HSPCs, whose deficiency, together with diabetes-associated epigenetic modifications, enhanced chromatin accessibility and expression of genes involved in myeloid leukocyte differentiation. Consequently, this led to myeloid leukocyte-biased differentiation of HSPCs at the expense of erythroid lineage. Pharmacological upregulation of Nur77 with its agonist cytosporone B (Csn-B) effectively prevented anemia in diabetic mice. Clinically, Nur77 levels in HSPCs of diabetic patient negatively correlated with anemia occurrence. Collectively, our findings reveal a novel Nur77-mediated pathway in diabetic anemia pathogenesis and propose Nur77 as a new therapeutic target.

records.title: International Cross-Age Consensus Guideline on Measurable Residual Disease Assessment in Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
records.abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) assessment is central to risk stratification, response evaluation, and relapse detection in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). However, substantial global variability in its methodology and implementation persists. Differences in sampling strategies, detection methods, reporting thresholds, and interpretation criteria hinder cross-trial comparability and clinical standardization. To address this, an international expert panel representing major pediatric and adult study groups and reference laboratories developed consensus recommendations, using a structured current-practices survey followed by a multi-round Delphi process. Consensus was achieved on 38 of 41 statements. Recommendations span three domains: pre-analytical requirements, technical and nomenclature standards, and MRD-based remission and relapse definitions. Bone marrow was endorsed as the reference specimen for MRD assessment, and MRD was prioritized over cytomorphology in cases of discordance. Principles for risk- and actionability-guided late MRD monitoring, confirmation of MRD reappearance, and MRD-informed relapse assessment were also defined. Among the key technical consensus statements, a standardized MRD assay nomenclature was adopted. Areas without consensus-namely, anticoagulant choice for PCR-based MRD, interpretation of isolated BCR::ABL1 reconversion, and the exclusive use of MRD to define remission-highlight ongoing biological and clinical complexity. This guideline, applicable across all ages, provides a practical framework to standardize MRD assessment in ALL and support MRD-guided clinical decision-making.

records.title: Pivekimab sunirine and the evolving treatment of blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm
records.abstract: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) is a rare hematologic malignancy characterized by leukemic blasts with frequent cutaneous involvement and high CD123 expression. Pivekimab sunirine, an anti-CD123 antibody-drug conjugate with a DNA-alkylating payload, was approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration on May 27, 2026, for adults with BPDCN based on the CADENZA study. We review its mechanism, clinical efficacy, toxicity, and role in the evolving treatment landscape for BPDCN and AML.

records.title: CAR-T Targeting of Mutant Calreticulin Selectively Eradicates Myeloproliferative Neoplasm-Sustaining Stem Cells
records.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) arise from and are sustained by hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) that acquire a driver mutation. Existing therapies fail to eliminate MPN HSCs, leaving allogeneic HSC transplantation (HSCT) as the only curative option. However, allogeneic HSCT non-selectively ablates both healthy and MPN HSCs, requiring donor stem-cell replacement and risking serious toxicities and death. MPN driver mutations in calreticulin (CALRmut) generate a shared C-terminal neopeptide unique to MPN cells that must be displayed at the cell surface in complex with the thrombopoietin receptor MPL to drive oncogenic signaling. These features make CALRmut an attractive target for selective immunotherapy. However, it is unknown whether MPN HSCs consistently display surface CALRmut to enable selective elimination in vivo via CALRmut targeting. We generated hAB2, a high-affinity CALRmut-specific humanized antibody, to use as the binding domain for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells. We show that functional murine and human MPN HSCs express surface CALRmut that is reliably detected by AB2 in vitro and in vivo. We developed an MPN patient-derived tumor xenograft (PDTX) model to enable rigorous testing of human MPN HSC-directed therapies in vivo. hAB2 CAR-T cells selectively eliminate CALRmut MPN HSCs in PDTX, eradicating all detectable MPN-propagating function in serial transplantation assays, while preserving co-existing normal human and host hematopoiesis. These findings establish cell-surface CALRmut display as a therapeutically exploitable feature of MPN HSCs and support the feasibility of CALRmut-targeted, transplant-free immunotherapies with curative intent for CALRmut MPNs.

records.title: Aligning Clinical Trial Reporting: A systematic analysis and position statement by the International Consortium for MDS
records.abstract: Variability in how clinical trial elements are reported can hinder accurate interpretation and comparison of trial results. Here, we systematically analyzed published manuscripts of therapeutic clinical trials in myelodysplastic syndromes/neoplasms (MDS) focusing on how key data elements were reported and made recommendations on how to improve this reporting. We included peer-reviewed full text manuscripts that reported results of clinical trials in MDS and were published between January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2024. We analyzed the presence or absence of several pre-determined key reporting elements and then synthesized these data to evaluate for consistency across manuscripts. We identified substantial variability in descriptions of patient characteristics, as well as the definitions used for response criteria. For example, baseline ANC was reported in only 16% of lower-risk MDS studies and 23% of higher-risk MDS studies, while baseline bone marrow blast percentage was reported in only 55% of higher-risk MDS manuscripts. In addition, response endpoints lacked standardization, with six unique definitions of RBC transfusion independence identified in lower-risk MDS trials and seven different definitions of overall response rate identified in higher-risk MDS trials. Informed by the results of this analysis, we then performed a modified-Delphi process for members of the International Consortium for MDS (icMDS) to develop consensus-based recommendations for consistent and accurate reporting of MDS clinical trial results. We advocate that these recommendations serve as benchmarks and templates for clinical trial reporting in MDS to improve interpretability and comparison of results.

records.title: Optimizing Reduced-Intensity Conditioning for Older Patients with AML and MDS: A Large-Scale Analysis from the CIBMTR
records.abstract: The optimal reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC) regimen for older patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (AHCT) remains undefined. We utilized CIBMTR registry data (2013-2022) to compare five common fludarabine-based regimens in 11,731 patients aged ≥50 years: fludarabine combined with 2 days of busulfan (FB2), melphalan 100 mg/m² (FM100), melphalan 140 mg/m² (FM140), or 2 Gy TBI with (FCT) or without (FT) cyclophosphamide. Using propensity score inverse probability weighting and Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART), we found that Fludarabine-melphalan (FM) regimens demonstrated superior long-term survival. Although FM140, FCT, and FT showed higher early mortality (≤6 months) than FB2 (P=.036), both FM100 (HR 0.79) and FM140 (HR 0.77) achieved significantly better late (> 6 months) overall survival (OS), outperforming all other regimens (P<.0001). In the 2019-2022 cohort, FM100, FM140, and FCT provided improved disease-free survival (DFS) relative to FB2. Specifically, FM100 yielded superior DFS compared to FCT (P=0.002) and FT (P=0.007). FM-based conditioning consistently resulted in lower relapse rates (P<.0001) and improved late GVHD-free/relapse-free survival. While FM regimens faced higher early non-relapse mortality (NRM), this impact did not persist beyond 6 months. BART analysis confirmed that these survival and relapse benefits remained robust across various patient comorbidities. In conclusion, FM100 and FM140 provide superior long-term survival and DFS for older patients with AML/MDS by providing potent anti-leukemic activity that offsets higher early toxicity. These findings support FM-based RIC as the preferred conditioning platform for this population, regardless of baseline comorbidities.

records.title: Microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids control cGVHD development by regulating antibody production
records.abstract: Chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) contributes substantially to morbidity and mortality in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. Microbe-derived short-chain fatty acids (SCFA) exert diverse local effects on the intestinal mucosa. We previously reported that a relative deficiency of SCFA in the circulation of transplant patients was associated with an increased incidence of cGVHD. We therefore hypothesized that circulating SCFA were unrecognized immunomodulators, generating protective effects after transplantation. We examined the role of SCFA butyrate and propionate in mouse models of cGVHD and now report that systemic administration of either butyrate or propionate mitigates cGVHD and improves survival. Exogenous SCFA treatment reduced pathogenic hyperexpanded B cells and recipient-specific IgA in the circulation, as well as decreasing the total alloantibody pool, defined using rapid extracellular antigen profiling (REAP). Our findings uncover a mechanism by which the intestinal microbiome plays a role in regulating antibody-dependent cGVHD pathogenesis and has implications for other antibody-mediated pathologies.

records.title: Etentamig in Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma: Pooled Phase 1 Data of an Investigational BCMA Bispecific Antibody
records.abstract: Etentamig is an investigational B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager, composed of a low-affinity CD3 binding domain, potentially reducing cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and infections, a high-avidity bivalent BCMA-binding domain, and retained FcRn binding supporting monthly (Q4W) dosing after a single step-up dose (SUD). We report long-term efficacy and safety from the ongoing, open-label, phase 1 (dose escalation/expansion; NCT03933735) and Arm A of the phase 1b (NCT05650632) studies of etentamig in adult patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, triple-class exposure, and ≥3 prior lines of therapy (LoT). In phase 1, patients received etentamig 60 mg Q4W or 40 mg Q3W, and in phase 1b, a SUD on Day 1 and 60 mg Q4W on Day 4. Among 146 patients (median age: 68 years; median [range] prior LoT: 4 [3-23]), median follow-up was 13 months (range: 1-48). Objective responses and ≥ very good partial responses occurred in 66% and 54% of patients. Median duration of response and progression-free survival were not reached. Pooled data suggest etentamig has a manageable safety profile, with Grade 3/4 neutropenia and infection occurring in 38% and 23% of patients. In phase 1b Arm A (n=23), overall CRS incidence was 30% (26% Grade 1; 4% Grade 2) with modified dexamethasone premedication and 1 SUD; median onset was 22.3 hours (range: 5.5-29.6) hours, with resolution in 20.7 hours (range: 1.8-131.7). Etentamig's molecular design may be associated with the observed clinical efficacy and tolerability while also potentially supporting extended dosing intervals.

records.title: CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM GRAFT VERSUS HOST DISEASE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: MECHANISTIC PATHWAYS AND THERAPEUTIC TARGETS
records.abstract: The development of graft versus host disease (GVHD) in the central nervous system (CNS) is a recognized complication that can lead to significant morbidity and mortality in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. In this article, we describe clinical manifestations and elucidate some of the diagnostic challenges associated with this disease entity. We then summarize new experimental insights that have emerged largely from pre-clinical murine studies that have investigated the pathophysiology of CNS GVHD. We delineate the vascular and lymphatic systems that regulate ingress and egress of soluble mediators and cellular populations, thereby functioning as specialized barriers that shield the brain under normal homeostatic conditions, and how these barriers are disrupted during GVHD-induced peripheral immune dysregulation. We also review pre-clinical studies that have uncovered mechanistic neuroinflammatory pathways involving cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α), cell surface receptors (type 2 cannabinoid receptor, colony stimulating factor-1 receptor) expressed on adaptive and innate immune cells, and antibiotic-induced gastrointestinal tract dysbiosis that have pathophysiological roles in this disorder. In addition, we provide evidence derived from these pre-clinical studies that the therapeutic targeting of individual pathways to attenuate CNS GVHD does not necessarily produce concordant responses in peripheral GVHD target organs, highlighting that the brain is a compartmentalized tissue site with a distinct microenvironment and supporting a more nuanced view of GVHD biology across CNS and non-CNS regions. Finally, we examine alternate therapeutic strategies to restore barrier integrity and thereby reduce T cell trafficking into the CNS to attenuate GVHD-associated neuroinflammation.

records.title: Regenerative Stress Contributes to Higher Clonal Hematopoiesis with Myelodysplastic Features in Sickle Cell Disease Mice
records.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) affects millions globally, causing significant lifelong morbidity and early death. As childhood mortality is reduced and SCD patients are surviving to adulthood, increased risk of hematological malignancy (HM) is becoming evident. Risk of therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS)/acute myeloid leukemia, following gene therapy or hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) is also higher in SCD. The specific pathobiology that predisposes to HM is necessary to address, since survival has improved and gene therapy and HSCT are being increasingly used. We modelled the increased risk of HM in humanized SCD mice, compared to age-, sex- and strain-matched normal counterparts. We serially monitored hematopoiesis in blood and bone marrow up to 1-year-of-age and performed highly sensitive, error-corrected deep sequencing of 450 MDS/HM-associated genes. Unlike controls, SCD mice showed an 'ageing-like' phenotype with premature development of myeloid-biased hematopoiesis and hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPC) mutational profile characteristic of aged mice/humans. Furthermore, a high proportion of SCD mice developed hematopoiesis with dysplastic features reminiscent of MDS morphology and higher clonal hematopoiesis burden. Imposition of regenerative stress by serial HSCT further increased HSPC mutational burden, resulting in evolution/expansion of clones harboring oncogenic driver mutations. Our study indicates that increased HSC regenerative stress, imposed either by chronic erythropoietic demand or via autologous HSCT in SCD increases the risk of developing clonal hematopoiesis and MDS-like features. Our study provides insights into a mechanism underlying increased risk of HM in this non-malignant hematological disorder, and suggests that early intervention with curative therapies may circumvent this risk.

records.title: Carfilzomib-based strategies in transplant-eligible multiple myeloma: long-term follow-up of the phase 2 FORTE trial
records.abstract: In the phase 2 FORTE trial, transplant-eligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma patients aged ≤65 years were randomized to (R1) carfilzomib-lenalidomide-dexamethasone followed by autologous stem cell transplantation (KRd-ASCT), twelve cycles of KRd (KRd12), or carfilzomib-cyclophosphamide-dexamethasone followed by ASCT (KCd-ASCT). Eligible patients were then randomized (R2) to maintenance with carfilzomib for 2 years plus lenalidomide until progression (KR) or lenalidomide alone until progression (R). With extended follow-up (median 99 months from R1 and 85 months from R2), KRd-ASCT significantly increased progression-free survival (PFS, median 98 months) versus KRd12 (median 70 months; HR 0.71, p=0.027) and KCd-ASCT (median 67 months; HR 0.66, p=0.006). A significant benefit in PFS2 was also observed versus both KRd12 (HR 0.65, p=0.02) and KCd-ASCT (HR 0.68, p=0.04) and in terms of overall survival (OS) versus KCd-ASCT (8-year OS: 76% vs 68%; HR 0.65, p=0.04). KR maintenance significantly improved PFS versus R (HR 0.67, p=0.02), with a time-dependent effect persisting up to two years after carfilzomib discontinuation; no differences in PFS2/OS were observed. KR significantly increased rate of measurable residual disease (MRD) conversion (sHR 0.47, p=0.03) during active treatment, and reduced MRD resurgence (sHR 0.53, p=0.001) versus R. Median duration of MRD negativity was 50.5 months in KR vs. 38 months in R arm. MRD-negative patients had significantly prolonged PFS with KR (HR 0.60, p=0.031); MRD-positive patients benefited from KR mainly during carfilzomib therapy (HR 0.46, p=0.05). The cumulative incidence of second primary malignancies was 6%. In conclusion, long-term follow-up confirms the high effectiveness of KRd-ASCT and KR maintenance. NCT02203643

records.title: Cytokines to modulate CAR T cells
records.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of B-cell malignancies, but insufficient expansion and persistence, progressive T-cell dysfunction, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments continue to limit durable efficacy and broader application. Cytokines are central regulators of both T-cell fitness and interactions with surrounding immune cells, providing a rationale for incorporating cytokine signals directly into engineered cellular therapies. Here we trace the development and clinical translation of cytokine-enhanced CAR T cells from the pioneering studies with IL-12 to common g-chain cytokines and IL-18. IL-12 established the potential of engineered T cells to deliver potent inflammatory signals locally and mobilize endogenous immunity, but also revealed the risk of systemic inflammatory toxicity. Common g-chain cytokines, particularly IL-7, IL-15 and IL-21, have predominantly been exploited to promote expansion, persistence and favorable differentiation states, with several approaches advancing to clinical testing. IL-18 combines direct support of engineered T cells with recruitment and remodeling of endogenous immune compartments and has recently demonstrated encouraging clinical activity in hematologic malignancies. Emerging strategies increasingly extend beyond cytokine secretion to inducible circuits, synthetic cytokine receptors, unconventional cytokines and combinations of complementary signals. Rational selection of cytokines for specific disease contexts, together with precise spatial and temporal control of their activity, will be critical to balance efficacy against toxicity and realize the full potential of cytokine-engineered cellular therapies.

records.title: Identification of a specialized lipid barrier for Drosophila metamorphosis
records.abstract: Many terrestrial insects transition from humid to dry environments at metamorphosis, yet how they avoid dehydration is unclear. In Drosophila melanogaster , we identify a lipid barrier to water loss in the pupa that is anatomically distinct from that of the adult. It comprises unisex hydrocarbons that are longer and less volatile than their sex-specific adult counterparts. These hyperlong hydrocarbons are produced by larval oenocytes and stored in the fat body for subsequent transport to the cuticle at pupariation. A fatty acid elongase, EloHL, is required for hyperlong hydrocarbon biosynthesis and for a functional barrier to dehydration during early metamorphosis. Hyperlong barrier hydrocarbons are widespread across the Drosophila genus and typically transition to shorter sex-specific versions during adult maturation. In the desert species D. mojavensis , however, adults retain hyperlong hydrocarbons. This study reveals how insect lipid barriers are tuned to environmental variations in aridity and temperature during development and evolution.

records.title: Brainstem enkephalinergic neural circuit underlying cold-induced pain relief in mice
records.abstract: Application of cold or cold-mimicking chemicals to injury has long been recognized as an effective means of pain relief. However, underlying neural mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified a cold-responsive neuronal subset within the lateral parabrachial nucleus (lPBN), the thermosensory relay region in the hindbrain, that mediates cold-induced analgesia in mice. Activation of these neurons and their projection to ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG) increased the nociceptive threshold, while ablation of these neurons attenuated analgesia induced by cold-mimicking chemicals. We further identified that these neurons express precursor gene of enkephalin ( Penk ), which is necessary for TRPM8 (transient receptor potential melastatin 8)–mediated pain relief. Mechanistically, cold-responsive lPBN neurons frequency-dependently released enkephalin peptide into vlPAG to activate the descending pain modulation circuitry via disinhibition. Activation of cold-responsive neurons reduced spinal cord responses to noxious stimuli, suggesting the involvement of a top-down pain modulation pathway. These findings propose a central mechanism underlying cold-induced pain relief, which could be a novel therapeutic target.

records.title: Pink noise in dyads’ semantic similarity trajectories predicts conversation enjoyment
records.abstract: Conversation is a core component of human social life. Many influential theories treat conversation as a linear system, i.e., the sum of its parts. However, linear accounts of semantic entrainment lose explanatory power at their upper limits: Discussing perfectly aligned opinions becomes boring. We propose an alternate account that considers the multiscale organization of semantic similarity over the course of a conversation, as indexed by pink noise. Here, we test whether pink noise can be found in interlocutors’ conavigated trajectories through semantic space. Not only is pink noise present, but its strength predicts positive conversation outcomes like enjoyment and connection, increases with practice, and is reflected in a large language model’s representation of conversation quality. These results demonstrate an important role for scale-free dynamics in characterizing successful conversation.

records.title: Mevalonate pathway regulates double-negative regulatory T cell stability in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease
records.abstract: Lipid metabolism dysfunction and immune imbalance are critical pathogenic drivers of metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Double-negative regulatory T cells (DNTreg) are important immune regulatory cells that maintain liver immune homeostasis. However, their survival and function are compromised in MASLD. Herein, we found that mevalonate pathway and its rate-limiting enzyme HMG-CoA reductase (HMGCR) were significantly down-regulated in DNTreg from both mice and patients with MASLD, correlating with impaired DNTreg viability and immunosuppressive function. Arachidonic acid is enriched in MASLD liver and inhibits DNTreg HMGCR expression. Geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP), a downstream product of HMGCR, mediates RAC1 geranylgeranylation, which facilitates its interaction with mitochondrial CLPX protease, thereby enhancing mitochondrial function and immunoregulatory activity of DNTreg. Adoptive transfer of Pggt1b +/− DNTreg into MASLD mice demonstrated significantly diminished therapeutic efficacy compared with wild-type DNTreg. In conclusion, mevalonate metabolism–mediated geranylgeranylation is essential for the suppressive activity and immune homeostasis of DNTreg in MASLD.

records.title: Temporal dynamics of antigen-specific T cell expansion in primary SARS-CoV-2 infection
records.abstract: Quantifying T cell response during primary infection in humans is crucial for understanding adaptive immunity. Leveraging a controlled human challenge to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, we characterized antigen-specific T cell responses within and across individuals. Notably, individual clones reached similar maximum frequencies despite differences in the timing of their peak expansion. Mathematical modeling within a coarse-grained framework suggested that variability in precursor frequency between different T cell clones could be one mechanism to explain this relationship. Single-cell profiling revealed distinct temporal programs for CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, with CD4 + cells expanding earlier but contracting to a lower frequency. Clones with similar receptors, likely recognizing the same antigen, expanded at similar times. Together, these findings highlight how clone-intrinsic properties such as precursor frequency and CD4/CD8 subset status shape T cell clonal kinetics. These insights provide a quantitative framework for understanding T cell response in humans, with implications for vaccine design.

records.title: Humid periods over western Sahara during the Middle Miocene Climate Transition and their implications on the carbon cycle
records.abstract: The Middle Miocene expansion of the Antarctic Ice Sheet coincides with major sedimentological changes in Malta. This interval also saw reorganisations in ocean circulation linked to closure of the Mesopotamian Seaway (MSR-events) and perturbations in the carbon cycle (CM events). The final CM event (CM-6), slightly lags the main glacial phase and remains difficult to interpret due to competing mechanisms and conflicting p CO 2 reconstructions. To explore links between cryosphere, circulation, hydroclimate, and the carbon cycle, we present new geochemical records from Malta. Our records show that cryospheric expansion was followed by large, precessionally paced variations in sea-surface salinity and a marked regional increase in biological productivity. The results indicate a shift toward stronger monsoonal influence, delivering enhanced freshwater and nutrient fluxes to the region. This enhanced local biological carbon pump may have acted as a positive feedback to a global CO 2 drawdown. However, any contribution to global CO 2 drawdown remains tentative and cannot be confirmed without contemporaneous high-resolution open-ocean records.

records.title: Revisiting the additionality and durability of carbon uptake in large-scale ocean iron fertilization
records.abstract: Climate stabilization pathways limiting global warming to 1.5° to 2°C require rapid emission reductions alongside additional carbon dioxide removal (CDR) of ∼2 to 3 PgC year −1 . Our simulations show that sustained century-scale ocean iron fertilization (OIF) in the southern sector of the Southern Ocean (SSO) provides a contribution of ∼30 PgC, equivalent to ∼0.3 PgC year −1 . This uptake nearly matches the additional carbon uptake from global fertilization. In other iron-limited regions, fertilization-induced uptake is largely offset (70 to 100%) by anomalous outgassing in nonfertilized regions. After terminating OIF following 30 years of fertilization, the ocean retains ∼50% of the additional carbon in the SSO, whereas retention is negligible elsewhere. These results identify the SSO as the most favorable region for durable carbon removal through large-scale OIF, particularly in terms of additionality and durability, although its carbon uptake is smaller than earlier estimates. Incomplete macronutrient drawdown reflects the uptake controls by light, top-down controls, and rates of macronutrient resupply. records.title: A transcriptional and cellular exploration of obesity and type II diabetes in human adipose tissues
records.abstract: Obesity is tightly linked to metabolic disorders such as type II diabetes mellitus (T2D), although a subpopulation of individuals with obesity do not present with these morbidities. The biological factors conferring T2D vulnerability remain incompletely understood. We recruited 58 individuals with obesity with or without a clinical diagnosis of T2D (Ob + T2D and Ob). We profiled paired samples of omental and subcutaneous adipose by single-cell RNA sequencing ( n = 10), flow cytometry under basal and stimulated conditions ( n = 42), and histology ( n = 17). Flow cytometry and chemokine quantification were also performed in paired whole blood. We identified reprogramming of the omental stromal compartment, centered on mesothelial and endothelial cells, alongside contrasting innate T cell and macrophage phenotypes across depots. Mesothelial and IGFBP2 + cells exhibited a fibrotic, epithelial-mesenchymal transition–like phenotype, while omental endothelial cells exhibited a lipid-overload, inflammatory, antigen presentation profile in T2D. Omental and subcutaneous adipose innate T cells exhibited divergent inflammatory profiles between tissues. These findings reveal previously unidentified insights into the pathophysiology of T2D in adipose tissue and identify compensatory networks within the tissues that could be exploited by targeted therapeutics.

records.title: Comprehensive degron mapping in human transcription factors
records.abstract: Gene expression is regulated by the targeted degradation of transcription factors through the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Transcription factors destined for degradation are recognized by E3 ubiquitin-protein ligases through motifs termed degrons, embedded within the sequence. In this study, we systematically map degrons in all 1626 human transcription factors. We find thousands of both known and previously unidentified degrons and characterize their sequence properties. Active degrons placed within exposed and intrinsically disordered regions contribute to modulating the abundance of the transcription factors, while the most common somatic mutations that are linked to skin cutaneous melanoma lead to unfolding and exposure of a latent degron buried in the zinc finger structure. We present examples of compartment-specific degrons and demonstrate that variant effects in transcription factors correlate with degron potency. Last, we show that while >60% of all predicted transcriptional activation domains overlap with strong degrons, acidic residues within the remaining transactivating regions counter the degron potency, showing how degrons can shape the transcription factor sequence landscape.

records.title: Shape-memory scaffold targets inflammation and fibrosis to restore endometrium and fertility in intrauterine adhesions
records.abstract: Intrauterine adhesion (IUA) is a major cause of infertility, yet current treatments remain limited in preventing fibrosis and restoring functional endometrium. Proteomic profiling of chemical, mechanical, and combined injury models revealed inflammatory activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and impaired regenerative programs, providing a molecular rationale for combining epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) with 17β-estradiol (E 2 ). BiSMR couples an E 2 -loaded PLTG [poly( l -lactide)- co -trimethylene carbonate- co -glycolic acid] backbone with a PDA-EGCG@HAMA coating, enabling rapid EGCG release followed by sustained E 2 delivery. In vitro, BiSMR promoted cell proliferation, migration, angiogenesis, and M2 polarization while suppressing myofibroblast transition. In rat IUA models, BiSMR restored endometrial structure and vascularization, reduced fibrosis, and improved implantation and live birth rates. Proteomics revealed down-regulation of fibrosis- and inflammation-related effectors and restoration of protein biosynthesis and regenerative pathways. records.title: Ultrafast Meissner-levitated microrotor
records.abstract: Levitated mechanical systems offer a powerful and flexible platform for the realization of ultralow-noise sensors and tests of fundamental physics. Here, we report the demonstration of a levitated microrotor, consisting of a magnetic microsphere levitated by the Meissner effect at 4.2 kelvin. The rotor reaches rotation frequencies above 2.3 megahertz (138 million revolutions per minute) while exhibiting an exceptionally low damping rate of 4.75 × 10 −7 hertz. Exploiting the linear dependence of friction on the gas density, we demonstrate high-accuracy absolute pressure sensing over a wide range at cryogenic temperature. Last, we detect the thermal torque noise at intermediate pressure by operating the rotor in synchronized mode, resulting in a first preliminary narrowband search for axion-like dark matter. More broadly, the combination of high rotational speed, low temperature, and low thermal torque noise establishes a previously unidentified regime for precision measurements, with direct implications for the detection of extremely weak forces and fields.

records.title: Electron competition in azobenzene programs infection-adaptive antibacterial therapy
records.abstract: Conventional stimulus-responsive antibacterial systems generally operate through binary trigger–activation mechanisms, making them poorly suited to evolving infection microenvironments and thereby contributing to persistent infection and resistance development. Here, we establish an azobenzene-based kinetic regulatory system in which oxygen gradients commonly present in infected tissues continuously program reaction kinetics through electron competition. Oxygen acts as a competing electron acceptor within the reductive reaction network, partitioning electron transfer between azo reduction and oxygen consumption. Substituent electronic structures further reshape reduction propensity, encoding distinct kinetic behaviors. These electronically programmed kinetics translated into adaptive nanoscale dissociation and drug-release profiles: Electron-rich azobenzenes rapidly disassembled under severe hypoxia, whereas electron-withdrawing structures sustained release under mild hypoxia, generating infection state–adaptive antibacterial outputs. Moreover, the same electronic features governing reduction kinetics also reduced the reactivity and toxicity of reductive metabolites. This work establishes electron competition as a strategy for converting environmental gradients into continuous kinetic outputs for adaptive antibacterial therapy.

records.title: Explainable AI identifies recombination and chromatin environment as key predictors of subgenome evolution in maize and Brassica
records.abstract: Polyploidy, or whole genome duplication, reshapes genomes through biased gene loss and regulatory rewiring, yet the drivers of biased fractionation among subgenomes remain unclear. In both species, eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) approaches identified recombination rate as the most influential and highly interconnected feature despite nonsignificant mean differences between subgenome groups. Chromosome location, transposon density, and chromatin-associated features, including the proximity of accessible chromatin regions to genes and active histone marks such as H3K9ac and H3K27ac, consistently ranked among the top contributors to subgenome classification. XAI-derived covariation and interaction networks further revealed recombination rate as the central node connecting significant features. Together, these results highlight recombination and chromatin environment as major predictors of subgenome divergence in polyploid genomes.

records.title: The (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide is a microbe-derived NAD + precursor that drives gut stem cell renewal
records.abstract: Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD) is a critical cellular coenzyme whose decline associates with various chronic and inflammatory diseases. Improved NAD restoration may reduce disease risks and extend healthy lifespan. We report here that certain commensal bacteria including specific probiotic species produce (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide (N-MNA), which is a structural isomer of methylnicotinamide, a nicotinamide degradative metabolite. Patients with gut dysbiosis and inflammation show reduced stool N-MNA. Stable isotope tracing revealed that N-MNA can be rapidly taken up and incorporated into NAD redox reactions by intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) and non-IECs of fruit fly, mouse, and human. Genetic and pharmacological analyses suggest that N-MNA is converted to NAD + via the Preiss-Handler pathway, independent of the salvage pathway. Cell-type-specific ablation or overexpression of SIRT1, an NAD-consuming enzyme, in Drosophila , along with intestinal stem cell (ISC) lineage tracing in mice revealed that systemic N-MNA supplementation promotes ISC regeneration and gut epithelial repair. Compared to known NAD precursors, N-MNA brings a methyl group into host cells, representing a class of microbe-derived NAD precursor that stimulates the tissue regenerative power.

records.title: Combating drug-resistant Aeromonas veronii : Multiomics revealed the antibacterial mechanism of resveratrol
records.abstract: Aeromonas , widely distributed in aquatic ecosystems, is a prevalent fish pathogen and can cause human infections via contaminated aquatic products, polluted water contact, or tainted food consumption. Escalating antibiotic resistance in Aeromonas strains highlights an urgent need for alternative natural antimicrobial agents. This study investigated resveratrol’s antibacterial mechanisms against Aeromonas veronii and evaluated its protective efficacy in hybrid sturgeon. Resveratrol exhibited strong activity [minimum inhibitory concentration: 128 microgram per milliliter (μg/ml), minimum bactericidal concentration: 256 μg/ml], disrupting cell wall/membrane integrity, inducing reactive oxygen species accumulation, inhibiting adenosine 5′-triphosphate synthesis, and down-regulating key metabolic pathways via transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. These findings confirm resveratrol as a promising antibiotic alternative against A. veronii , with nanoemulsion formulation enhancing its therapeutic efficacy.

records.title: A robust spin-coupled tetraradical via nonalternant design
records.abstract: Polyradicals in open-shell polycyclic hydrocarbons (PHs) offer access to multiple spin states and hold great promise for spintronics and quantum technologies. Here we report a nonalternant, air-stable tetraradical featuring two fused 7-5-7 rings and a strongly correlated singlet ground state. This molecule displays an exceptional tetraradical character ( y 0 = 1.00, y 1 = 0.89) and exhibits long ambient stability ( t 1/2 = 33 days). Comprehensive electronic structure and magnetic response analyses reveal that the spin topology is governed by both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions, with robust electron correlation ( J 1 = +321 K, J 2 = −44 K, and J 3 = −29 K). The unique nonalternant design suppresses hyperfine and vibrational decoherence, giving rise to long spin relaxation and coherence time. These findings demonstrate that embedding nonalternant motifs into PH polyradicals provides a powerful strategy to simultaneously promote molecular stability, spin-exchange coupling, and spin robustness—key features for materials in the rising field of quantum information science.

records.title: Prebiotic magnetite enables chirality-magnetic surface feedback
records.abstract: The emergence of biomolecular homochirality requires both an initial symmetry-breaking event and a mechanism to amplify and preserve a chiral imbalance. Magnetic minerals have been shown to function as chiral agents through the chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect and may have enabled homochirality on early Earth, yet the magnetic properties of magnetite formed under realistic prebiotic conditions remain unexplored. Here, we show that magnetite synthesized through two geochemically plausible pathways—UV-driven photo-oxidation and nitrite-mediated oxidation of Fe(II)—produces particles dominated by single-vortex and multivortex magnetic domain states. Magnetic measurements and electron microscopy confirm that these populations differ markedly from the nano-fabricated thin-film substrates conventionally used in previous CISS experiments. Using three-dimensional micromagnetic simulations, we demonstrate that single-domain and vortex-state grains undergo irreversible, exchange-driven remagnetization when interacting with spin-polarized homochiral compounds. This magnetic irreversibility provides a robust mechanism for storing and reinforcing weak chiral bias, suggesting that prebiotic magnetite could have contributed to the emergence and stabilization of persistent chiral bias on early Earth.

records.title: Spatial proteomics reveals lipid droplet reorganization in symbiotic Paramecium bursaria cells
records.abstract: Endosymbiosis is an important adaptive mechanism allowing organisms to exploit previously inaccessible niches. The flexible relationship between the ciliate Paramecium bursaria and green algae represents a model system for studying early endosymbiosis evolution. However, the mechanisms underlying how P. bursaria cells maintain this endosymbiotic relationship remain unclear. Here, we use mass spectrometry–based proteomics to generate a spatial proteomic atlas of the host P. bursaria cells with and without endosymbionts. This atlas defines the protein composition of the endosymbiont-containing compartment (perialgal vacuole) and reveals pronounced remodeling of host lipid droplets upon symbiosis. Imaging analyses confirm that lipid droplets change in size, morphology, and positioning, accumulating near intracellular algae. Perturbing symbiotic cells with chemical inhibitors of lipid metabolism reduces endosymbiotic algal numbers, revealing a role for lipid droplets in the host-endosymbiont interaction. Our data provide a comprehensive resource for protein localization in P. bursaria cells and elucidate how those cells remodel an existing cellular compartment to maintain endosymbiosis.

records.title: Spatial control of enzyme orientation at the lipid droplet interface enables regio- and chemoselective metabolic flux
records.abstract: Precise spatial control over multienzyme cascade reactions is increasingly recognized as a design lever in synthetic biology for enhancing catalytic performance and directing metabolic flux. By emulating principles of cellular compartmentalization, synthetic scaffolds and engineered interfaces have emerged as powerful platforms to modulate intermediate channeling and reaction efficiency in complex biocatalytic systems. However, robust and spatially defined immobilization of multienzyme assemblies within physicochemically optimal compartments remains challenging because of the dynamic intracellular environment. Here, we reprogram the amphiphilic interface of yeast lipid droplets (LDs) as a programmable scaffold system to support regio- and chemoselective localization of enzymes. Guided by molecular dynamics simulations, we designed LD-anchoring motifs to direct the enzyme orientation at the LD monolayer interface, yielding cytosol-facing or LD inner-facing configurations. Using this designed LD-anchoring motif, we spatially reorganize a trienzyme cascade for prodeoxyviolacein (PDV) biosynthesis across the cytosol-LD interface, facilitating directional conversion of hydrophilic substrates into hydrophobic products. This spatial reorganization substantially improved PDV production by 1300%, achieving 46.25 milligrams per liter. Our approach offers a modular and tunable platform for engineering spatially organized and readily deployable enzyme cascades, opening avenues for biosynthetic catalysis at organellar interfaces.

records.title: Visualizing nanoscopic acoustic mode competition in a van der Waals ferroelectric
records.abstract: Understanding how low-dimensional ferroelectrics respond to ultrafast excitation at nanoscales is essential for controlling energy flow and mechanical functionality in next-generation polar devices, yet the nanoscopic structural response to ultrafast depolarization remains unresolved, obscuring the microscopic pathways of acoustic decoherence and energy dissipation. Here, we spatiotemporally resolve lattice motion in the van der Waals ferroelectric NbOI 2 using combined ultrafast electron microscopy and diffraction, revealing three acoustic phonons: two transverse shear modes and one longitudinal breathing mode. The transverse mode that shears the layers perpendicular to the in-plane polar axis dominates over that along the polar axis, reflecting anisotropic polarization-strain coupling. Real-space mapping uncovers spatially correlated heterogeneity in mode amplitudes and lifetimes. Regions dominated by a single shear mode exhibit significantly longer acoustic lifetimes than multimode regions, suggesting acoustic phonon–phonon scattering as a major source of decoherence. Our results provide a microscopic understanding of ultrafast depolarization-driven acoustic dynamics and spatially heterogeneous energy dissipation in van der Waals ferroelectrics.

records.title: Scaling up chemical recycling: High-yield polyolefin pyrolysis to liquid hydrocarbons using iron single atom catalysts
records.abstract: The chemical recycling of polyolefins (PO) via pyrolysis offers a circular pathway for plastic waste management, yet industrial implementation remains hindered by high energy demands and poor product selectivity. Here, we report an Fe-catalyzed pyrolysis process that achieves 97% PO conversion and a 94% yield of C6 to C35 liquid hydrocarbons. By using a zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF)–derived, N-doped porous carbon-supported iron single-atom catalyst (Fe 1 @NC) in combination with a strategic temperature gradient control, we overcome traditional thermolysis limitations. The process was further demonstrated on a kilogram scale, supporting the practical scalability of this catalytic system. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the rate-determining step is an acid base–promoted dehydrogenation of the polymer backbone. Specifically, electronic synergy between the single iron centers and the carbon support stabilizes reactive carbocation intermediates, facilitating their rapid decomposition into high-value olefins and alkanes. These findings provide a scalable and highly efficient catalytic framework for the upcycling of plastic waste into liquid hydrocarbon fractions and chemical feedstocks.

records.title: Adaptive dual-programming magnetic soft robot with lifelike behavior
records.abstract: Magnetic soft robots with embodied intelligence of multimodal motions, environmental perception, and functional decoupling depend on ingenious material arrangement and programmable morphing information introduction. While some efforts have been made, achieving lifelike behaviors for soft robots in system-level strategy remains a notable challenge. Here, we present dual-programming hydrogel-based soft robots (DHSRs) that couple magnetic and anisotropic programming through the spatial arrangement of patterned magnetic skeletons into responsive and structural hydrogel bodies. These DHSRs exhibit programmable exquisite and multicurved structures in three-dimensional (3D) space, environment-adaptive deformation behaviors proved by switching from random jumping on land to regular swimming in water of a fish-like soft robot, and further locomotion-function decoupling capabilities of region-selective cargo delivery in an integrated “locomotion-perception-action” workflow. Our strategy in biomedical potential is exemplified by a ring-like pH-responsive DHSR for gastric ulcer therapy, which integrates multimodal locomotion (rolling, tumbling, and rotating), adaptive matching, and microneedle-mediated penetration. By collaborating with a capsule endoscopy system, we explore the possibility of a wireless and painless diagnostic-therapeutic platform in a pig model. This strategy endows the robot with perception and multitask execution capabilities, highlighting a promising route for the intelligent evolution of soft robots across diverse application domains.

records.title: Age reshapes selection on melanoma driver mutations
records.abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for melanoma. However, it is unclear whether aging fuels tumor evolution by altering mutation rates, changing the microenvironmentally induced selection on drivers, or both. We analyzed 5472 melanomas, estimating how selection on individual variants changes with patient age while accounting for differing neutral mutation rates. Neutral mutation rates increased only modestly with age; ultraviolet damage remained predominant, but endogenous processes increasingly contributed to older tumors. In contrast, selection on major drivers was strongly age dependent: The advantage of BRAF V600E declined precipitously with age, whereas NRAS Q61 mutations gained advantage. TERT promoter mutations became more frequent, yet less advantageous. Aging therefore reshapes melanoma evolution primarily by altering selection, motivating age-conscious evaluation of clinical biomarkers and therapies.

records.title: Measuring mixed-state topological invariant in open photonic quantum walk
records.abstract: Pure-state manifestations of geometric phase are well established and have found applications across essentially all branches of physics, yet their generalization to mixed-state regimes remains largely unexplored experimentally. The Uhlmann geometric phase offers a natural extension of pure-state paradigms and can exhibit a topological character. However, observation of this invariant is impeded by the incompatibility between Uhlmann parallel transport and Hamiltonian dynamics, as well as the difficulty of preparing topologically nontrivial mixed states. To address this challenge, we report an experimentally accessible protocol for directly measuring the mixed-state topological invariant. By engineering controlled nonunitary dynamics in a photonic quantum walk, we prepare topologically nontrivial mixed states from a trivial initial state. Then, by machine learning the full density matrix in momentum space, we directly extract the quantized geometric phase of the nontrivial mixed states. Furthermore, we observe that this transition of the quantized mixed-state topological invariant from a trivial to a nontrivial value is closely associated with the emergence of a topological kink structure. These results highlight a geometric phase framework that naturally extends to open quantum systems both in and out of thermal equilibrium.

records.title: A full-hardware edge detection system based on a highly robust dual random number generator
records.abstract: Conventional edge computing hardware at autonomous driving terminals is limited by chip area and power efficiency for complex image data. Recently, researchers have used memristors to construct dedicated hardware systems, achieving advancements in multiple image processing fields such as pattern recognition and edge detection. However, a full-hardware image processing system with anti-interference, low power, and high real-time performance remains challenging. Here, we fabricated a volatile Ag/AlO x /n-Si memristor with exceptional stability and low power. High-resolution electron microscopy visualized Ag conductive filament formation. Integrating two memristors with a logic circuit, we designed a low-power edge detection unit using dual random number hardware computation. Its energy consumption is 92.3% lower than traditional logic circuits, with strong anti-interference. To validate practical use, we constructed a 32-channel parallel full-hardware system with 64 devices, achieving 31.25 frames per second and excellent edge detection. The system exhibits excellent scalability, stability, and anti-interference, offering great potential for edge vision hardware in autonomous driving, safety monitoring, and surgical assistance.

records.title: Photonic entanglement swapping with remote quantum dots
records.abstract: Entanglement swapping is a protocol that details how to create entanglement between previously uncorrelated particles. Its photonic version, mediated by the interference of photon pairs generated by separate quantum systems, finds disparate applications in quantum networks. So far, entanglement swapping with entangled photons from remote systems has been implemented only using probabilistic sources. However, the scaling up of quantum networks requires nonprobabilistic quantum emitters without a trade-off between the degree of entanglement and photon-pair generation rate. Here, we demonstrate photonic entanglement swapping using photon pairs generated by two separate GaAs quantum dots. The emitters are deterministically embedded in hybrid semiconductor-piezoelectric devices that make the entangled photons from two dissimilar quantum dots nearly identical. Entanglement swapping is demonstrated with a fidelity as high as 0.71(2), more than 10 SDs above the classical limit. The experimental data are quantitatively explained by a theoretical model that also suggests how to boost the protocol performance. Our work opens the path to the exploitation of quantum dot entangled-photon sources in quantum repeater networks.

records.title: Three-way circulation–soil moisture–temperature feedbacks amplify the most extreme mid-latitudinal heat waves
records.abstract: The most extreme heat waves are intensifying faster than moderate events across many mid-latitude regions. Climate models underestimate these trends, suggesting an incomplete representation and understanding of the underlying physical processes. Here, we use an explainable machine-learning framework to investigate interactions among atmospheric circulation, surface soil moisture, and temperature, and their role in recent heat extremes. We show that a three-way interaction among these components becomes active once a critical temperature threshold is exceeded, contributing, on average, ∼10% to peak temperature anomalies during the most extreme heat events across ∼28% of humid mid-latitude regions. We further reveal that this interaction is systematically underestimated in CMIP6 and CESM2 Large Ensemble simulations. Soils in climate models are too dry at the initiation of heat waves, therefore suppressing subsequent soil-moisture depletion and inhibiting feedback activation. These findings help explain regional model biases in upper-tail warming and highlight avenues for improving future projections of extreme heat events.

records.title: Quantum-interference metrology of dissipative Kerr solitons
records.abstract: Dissipative Kerr solitons in optical microresonators underpin chip-scale frequency combs with applications ranging from coherent telecommunications to precision spectroscopy. Yet the characterization of their intrinsic femtosecond temporal structure remains challenging, as the low pulse energy and broad spectral bandwidth necessitate optical amplification and careful dispersion compensation in conventional ultrafast diagnostics, both of which can substantial distort the waveform. Here, we demonstrate a quantum-interference metrology of microcomb solitons based on Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. By attenuating the soliton stream to the single-photon level and measuring fourth-order interference, we directly retrieve near transform-limited pulse durations without amplification or dispersion management, remaining accurate even after propagation through 25 kilometers of standard fiber. The same interferogram also provides direct access to the temporal separations in multisoliton states by converting intersoliton separations into additional interference dips at corresponding delays, enabling subpicosecond characterization of their intracavity temporal structure. This quantum-inspired paradigm introduces a metrological approach that is immune to amplification and dispersion distortions, offering a powerful tool for the characterization of complex soliton physics.

records.title: Structure of the Chimalliviridae bacteriophage Goslar reveals host recognition and infection machinery

Here, we use cryo–electron microscopy to determine a structure of the Escherichia coli –infecting Chimalliviridae phage Goslar. We combine manual modeling of 25 structural proteins with AlphaFold structure predictions of an additional three proteins to generate a composite model with 2888 protein chains from 28 different structural proteins, totaling more than 1.4 million amino acid residues. Our structure reveals the architecture of the Goslar capsid, portal, tail, and baseplate, highlighting structural similarities and differences with other tailed phages. Combining our structural data with quantitative mass spectrometry of Goslar virions, we identify several high-copy virion-associated proteins that likely play key roles when injected into host cells upon infection. We also identify a Chimalliviridae -specific family of proteins that form long, flexible filaments anchored at the phage baseplate and which incorporate carbohydrate-binding domains, suggesting a key role in host recognition.

records.title: Reciprocal control of genome instability and RNA processing in cancer: Mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities
records.abstract: Genomic instability and dysregulated RNA processing are each recognized as core hallmarks of cancer, but accumulating evidence indicates that they are mechanistically intertwined rather than independent features. Chromosomal instability, mismatch-repair deficiency, and homologous recombination deficiency can reshape RNA splicing, 3′ end formation, and RNA surveillance through changes in gene dosage, DNA damage signaling, and alterations in regulatory elements. Conversely, aberrant splicing, polyadenylation, and RNA modifications can impair DNA repair, perturb mitotic control, and promote replication stress, thereby reinforcing genomic instability. This bidirectional circuit drives clinically relevant phenotypes, including therapeutic resistance, immune modulation, and emergent vulnerabilities that are not captured by DNA-centric biomarkers alone. Here, we present a unified framework for the genome instability–RNA processing axis and its direct clinical implications for cancer diagnosis, treatment stratification, and therapeutic exploitation, highlighting the most actionable mechanistic interfaces and discussing how integrated DNA-RNA biomarkers and rational combination strategies could extend precision oncology beyond static genomic lesions.

records.title: High-impulse and reactant-regenerative combustion-based micro actuators
records.abstract: The use of combustibles in micro-actuator technologies enables powerful impulsive actuation capabilities comparable to those of natural organisms. However, the exogenous dependence of fuel limits the development of combustion-based actuators. We present a closed-cycle reactant regeneration strategy wherein the bidirectional interconversion between hydrogen and water achieves real-time fuel replenishment for reactant-regenerative electrolysis and combustion reactions. Based on this, we develop a 1.5-centimeter actuator that generates forces above 20 newtons and operates continuously for >7200 cycles without refueling (a two orders-of-magnitude improvement over existing combustion-based actuators). Experiments confirm its strength and cross-environment versatility for removing obstacles, jetting, and striking via underwater cavitation. These features enable the actuator to be integrated into small robotic platforms, allowing them to reconfigure local surroundings in an active manner.

The compounds show exceptional antiviral activity both in vitro and in vivo and protect against influenza illness in ferrets and in mice after a single dose, either therapeutically or prophylactically.

records.title: Strigolactone receptor D14 integrates phosphate and strigolactone signaling by interacting with and stabilizing PHR1
records.abstract: Strigolactone (SL) and low phosphate (LP) signaling coordinately regulate shoot and root architecture and plant adaptation. While LP signaling is generally considered upstream of SL biosynthesis, their interaction is more complex. For instance, exogenous SL exerts opposite effects on lateral root formation under low versus high phosphorus. Here, we show that under LP, SL-induced anthocyanin accumulation requires PHR1, demonstrating that PHR1 functions downstream of SL signaling. We uncovered an SL-dependent physical interaction between PHR1 and the SL receptor DWARF14 (D14). This interaction promotes PHR1 dimerization, stabilizes PHR1 by inhibiting its ubiquitination-mediated degradation, and enhances its transcriptional activation activity. The D14-PHR1 complex directly binds and up-regulates the SL biosynthesis gene MAX3 and anthocyanin biosynthesis genes, thereby inhibiting branching and hypocotyl elongation and promoting anthocyanin accumulation. These findings indicate that PHR1 mediates the coordination of SL and LP signaling, potentially explaining SL’s opposing effects on lateral root formation under different phosphorus conditions. In the phr1 mutant, exogenous SL inhibited lateral roots under both LP and Pi-sufficient conditions, confirming that the promoting role of SL under LP requires PHR1. PHR1 also interacted with D14 to activate LBDs and HB23 , regulating lateral root formation. records.title: Y chromosome instability in the early mouse embryo
records.abstract: The Y chromosome lacks canonical centromeric repeats necessary for high-fidelity chromosome segregation. In adult tissues, this causes Y loss and predisposes to disease. records.title: Basin-scale changes in net primary production from the biogeochemical-Argo array
records.abstract: Marine net primary production is expected to be affected by climate change. Although remote sensing offers broad spatial and temporal coverage, it is limited to surface observations and cannot capture subsurface variability. Autonomous profiling floats provide critical depth-resolved measurements that help bridge this gap. These changes, if occurring in response to climate forcing, raise concern due to the key role of phytoplankton productivity in sustaining marine ecosystems. These trends typically agree in direction and magnitude with those from satellites. Our findings highlight the value of the biogeochemical-Argo array in detecting change in ocean productivity, demonstrating its potential for sustained monitoring. These results underscore the need for integrated observing systems to capture the full extent of changing marine productivity.

records.title: A TROP2-targeting aptamer enables selective drug delivery and potent antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer

records.title: Nonlinear cooling and control of a mechanical quantum harmonic oscillator
records.abstract: Nonlinearities are a key feature allowing nonclassical control of quantum harmonic oscillators. However, when nonlinearities are strong, designing protocols for control is often difficult, placing a barrier to exploiting these properties fully. In this work, using a single trapped-ion oscillator operated in the strongly nonlinear regime of the atom-light interaction, we show how to generate localized multi (two, three, four, and five)–component Schrödinger’s cat manifolds using a novel form of nonlinear reservoir engineering. We then specifically select Hamiltonians which allow us to perform measurements on these state manifolds. Our work demonstrates the experimental use of high-order nonlinear processes for control of nonclassical states of a quantum harmonic oscillator, opening up a new toolbox which can be applied to bosonic quantum error correction, computation, and sensing.

records.title: Superoxide dismutase shapes manganese stoichiometry in Southern Ocean diatoms
records.abstract: Quantifying the elemental stoichiometry of marine phytoplankton biomass is crucial for projections of primary production. In many cases, the mechanistic underpinnings of biomass stoichiometry are unclear. We combined metaproteomics, Bayesian statistical modeling, and geochemical measurements to quantify the contribution of superoxide dismutases to metal stoichiometry in natural populations of Southern Ocean diatoms. Our analyses indicate that a substantial amount of manganese (Mn) in diatoms in an Antarctic polynya can be attributed to superoxide dismutases (∼0.7 micromoles of Mn:moles of carbon; ∼20% of the total cellular Mn quota). We then used proteomic profiles of polar diatom cultures to identify environmental controls on superoxide dismutases and found that Mn limitation induces the depletion of Mn superoxide dismutases and an accompanying increase in nickel superoxide dismutase. Overall, we combined metaproteomic approaches to quantify proteome composition and connected these measurements to metal-to-carbon ratios and their responses to metal availability. Our approach provides a mechanism for directly parameterizing ecosystem-scale models with molecular measurements.
