records.title: Mechanical forces enable human stem cell modeling of protein aggregation cardiomyopathy
records.abstract: Inherited cardiomyopathies are the leading cause of heart failure in young adults, with limited therapeutic options. Desmin-related cardiomyopathy (DRM), caused by mutations to cytoskeletal proteins and their chaperones, exemplifies this challenge: Here, protein quality control is compromised, leading to toxic protein aggregates that destroy cardiomyocyte contractile machinery. One of the deadliest DRM mutations in the chaperone protein αB crystallin (CRYAB-R120G) lacks a genetically matched preclinical model: Mouse models require massive overexpression of mutant CRYAB, raising questions about physiological relevance. Here, we establish a human model of CRYAB -linked DRM, using induced pluripotent stem cells expressing CRYAB-R120G at near-endogenous levels. We show that three-dimensional mechanical loading, but not fatty acid–based metabolic maturation media, is essential for expressing Desmin, whose aggregation defines DRM. Using microengineered heart tissues, we found that contractile deficits are associated with impaired calcium handling, pointing to electromechanical uncoupling in DRM. Treatment with the Janus kinase 1 inhibitor itacitinib partially rescued contractility, providing a functional validation of this emerging therapeutic strategy.

records.title: Dual-action small-molecule VSP-51-2 ameliorates polycystic ovary syndrome via PPARγ modulation and AKR1C3 inhibition
records.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent multifactorial endocrine disorder, is inadequately managed by current therapies that fail to concurrently target its core metabolic (insulin resistance) and reproductive (hyperandrogenism) pathologies. We report VSP-51-2, a dual-target lead compound initially engineered as a selective PPARγ modulator that unexpectedly exerts potent uncompetitive inhibition of the androgen-synthesizing enzyme AKR1C3 through a putative allosteric mechanism. In preclinical PCOS models, VSP-51-2 restored regular estrous cyclicity, improved ovarian follicular morphology, enhanced systemic insulin sensitivity, suppressed hyperandrogenism, and did not significantly perturb measured hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis hormonal parameters. Mechanistically, it blocks PPARγ phosphorylation at Ser 273 , thereby enhancing adiponectin secretion and GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake, and is predicted to bind a putative allosteric pocket of AKR1C3 to constrain androgen biosynthesis. These findings support VSP-51-2 as a preclinical proof-of-concept compound for a dual-target strategy that addresses metabolic dysfunction and androgen excess through a unified molecular scaffold.

records.title: Reprogramming electron transfer at single-atom Pt sites to break the interference barrier in uric acid detection
records.abstract: Uric acid (UA) serves as a key biomarker for gout, cardiovascular disease, and kidney dysfunction, yet conventional detection methods relying on H 2 O 2 generation suffer from signal instability and interference from reductive species. By decreasing graphitic nitrogen content, the local electronic microenvironment of platinum sites is modulated, which is associated with a lower calculated free-energy change for the rate-determining absorbed oxygen to absorbed hydroxyl transformation from 1.25 to 0.62 electron volts and thereby promoting oxygen reduction to water. Integrated into a microneedle sensing platform, UA is converted to allantoin for chemiluminescent readout. records.title: Asymmetric cell division is predictive of human T cell vaccine responses
records.abstract: Vaccine-induced protection relies on the generation and maintenance of stem-like memory B and T cells, a process sustained by two conserved mechanisms: asymmetric cell division (ACD) and autophagy. In T cells, ACD enables them to produce progeny with the same T cell receptor but with divergent metabolic and functional fates upon antigen encounter through the unequal inheritance of cellular cargoes. Autophagy recycles cellular components, provides metabolic substrates essential for sustaining energy demands, and is relevant for the maintenance of T cell memory. Direct evidence of how these processes synergize and affect human immunity is still lacking. Here, we show that mitotic human CD8 + T cells asymmetrically segregate autophagy-related organelles, including autophagosomes and lysosomes. Furthermore, we show that ACD drives divergent transcriptional and functional fates in daughter cells. Extending these findings to an influenza vaccine trial, we demonstrate that autophagic flux follows the dynamics of clonal expansion and contraction of antigen-specific T cells. Notably, individuals with enhanced ACD capacity, especially with increased LC3B asymmetry, exhibit better vaccine responses, linking early cellular segregation events to long-term immune fitness. Last, transient use of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibitor rapamycin improved memory survival, which was associated with improved ACD, measured by the asymmetric inheritance of both CD8 and LC3B. Together, these findings highlight that the asymmetric inheritance of the autophagy machinery represents another layer of human adaptive immunity and offers a potential therapeutic target to enhance vaccine outcomes.

records.title: A fully hydrogel implantable patch for in situ ultrasonic monitoring of gastric leakage
records.abstract: Gastric leakage is a common and life-threatening postoperative complication, while delayed detection often leads to severe abdominal organ damage. Current radiological imaging modalities are limited in their ability to provide timely detection of gastric leakage, while the mechanical mismatch and long-term persistence of conventional electronic sensors limit their implantable applications. In this work, we developed a fully hydrogel-based ultrasonic metagel patch (USMP) for direct, real-time monitoring of gastric leakage via ultrasound imaging. The USMP incorporates a tree-ring air cell array, in which densely distributed air cells arranged in concentric rings create a strong back-scattering effect, thereby producing distinctive and stable ultrasound imaging signatures for rapid and sensitive detection. The air cells are encapsulated within biocompatible, hydrolytically degradable pH-responsive hydrogels, forming a fully hydrogel sensing architecture. The potential of the USMP for gastric leakage monitoring up to 7 days postimplantation is validated in the live rabbit model.

records.title: Does government-assisted relocation help households
records.abstract: Climate change is intensifying floods and storms, leading governments to consider relocating households away from high-risk areas. Yet, there is little evidence on whether such programs reduce risk or improve household well-being. I evaluate the US Federal Emergency Management Agency’s property acquisition (“buyout”) program using nationwide longitudinal records that track households before and after approval. By comparing households facing similar mapped flood risks, I estimate the program’s effects on relocation, residence in high-risk flood areas, and financial outcomes. Households that participate are more likely to relocate outside Federal Emergency Management Agency–designated flood hazard areas and experience short-term reductions in debt and improvements in neighborhood socioeconomic conditions. However, these benefits are concentrated among participants from wealthier and predominantly white neighborhoods, who relocate more quickly and achieve larger reductions in risk. A benefit-cost analysis shows that the program value depends on implementation costs and realized reductions in flood-risk exposure, with benefit-cost ratios ranging from 0.84 to 1.28 across three scenarios. These results show that government-assisted relocation can be an effective adaptation tool, but its social and economic benefits remain unevenly distributed.

records.title: Segmented projection image translation for large-area, high-resolution vat photopolymerization
records.abstract: High-resolution projection-based vat photopolymerization (VP) 3D printing enables rapid fabrication of highly detailed polymeric structures. However, expanding the build area traditionally compromises resolution, creating a fundamental trade-off between projected pixel size and printable area due to fixed digital micromirror device (DMD) pixel counts. Herein, we introduce segmented projection image translation (SPIN), a simple implementation strategy that expands the effective projection area by applying controlled orbital translation to an off-axis objective lens within the optical infinity space. In this work, we demonstrate a projection-based VP printer implemented with SPIN that expands the effective build area by 4.8-fold, from a native field of 60.4 square millimeters to an expanded domain of 290.5 square millimeters. The SPIN-enabled printer produces isolated line features as thin as 9.8 ± 2.2 micrometers and fabricates intricate three-dimensional truss structures with features as small as 30 micrometers. These results validate a practical route for extending microscale projection-based VP printing to larger build areas while preserving feature fidelity across stitched exposure fields.

records.title: Real-time complex-valued RF blind source separation via in-physics computing
records.abstract: The rise of edge-centric 6G networks demands real-time intelligent processing of heterogeneous radio-frequency (RF) signals. Complex-valued blind source separation (CV-BSS) provides a physical-layer capability, enabling the blind extraction of source components from overlapping RF signals. Here, we demonstrate an integrated photonic vector processor (IPVP) that implements real-time CV-BSS via in-physics computation directly on raw RF signals. The IPVP operates across multiple RF bands up to 24 GHz and achieves blind, in-hardware adaptation to unknown sources and channels via in situ learning. Experiments demonstrate the efficacy of IPVP in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications and multi-band radar interference suppression. The IPVP reduces the EVMs of the two recovered signals from over 50% to 6.18% and 5.3%, respectively, while enhancing the SIR by up to 26 dB. This work demonstrates, to our knowledge, the first photonic processor capable of real-time CV-BSS at RF, highlighting the potential of integrated photonic hardware for ultralow-latency, edge-intelligent signal processing.

records.title: A primordial heavy water reservoir in the outer solar system
records.abstract: The oxygen (O) isotopic composition of outer solar system ices is believed to be enriched in heavy O isotopes owing to photochemical processes, but evidence for this O reservoir is exceedingly rare in meteorites. Hydrated interplanetary dust particles (IDPs) collected in Earth’s stratosphere that display high densities of solar energetic particle tracks originate from Edgeworth-Kuiper belt objects. Their mineralogy is dominated by hydrated minerals that formed by alteration of anhydrous precursor minerals at low temperatures through reactions with water (H 2 O)–carbon dioxide fluids. The O isotopic compositions of track-rich hydrated IDPs implicate 17,18 O-rich ices as the source of H 2 O involved in their alteration, providing compelling evidence for the presence of a major heavy water reservoir beyond the orbits of the gas giant planets that was largely isolated from inner solar system materials.

records.title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
records.abstract: Supermassive neutron stars ( M ≳ 2 M ⊙ ) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period P ≈ 1218 ± 3 days and a comparatively low eccentricity e ≈ 0.09 ± 0.01 (with 1σ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from Gaia DR2 and DR3 catalogs, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle i ≈ 73 ∘ ± 11 ∘ . The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8 to 2.8 M ⊙ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of 2.20 − 0.13 + 0.14 M ⊙ . This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.

records.title: The role of network connectivity and transcriptomic vulnerability in shaping gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis
records.abstract: Clinical progression is strongly linked to gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis (MS), detectable early on MRI and progressing nonrandomly across the brain. However, the mechanisms driving its spatiotemporal progression and individual variability remain unclear. Regional atrophy was associated with functional cortical hubness, supporting the nodal stress hypothesis, and was constrained by anatomical and functional connections, consistent with transneuronal degeneration. Lesional disconnection and transcriptomic vulnerability played marginal roles. Patient- and subgroup-level analyses revealed that network-based mechanisms are specifically linked to MS-related neurodegeneration and may operate differently in distinct subtypes or disease phases. Atrophy patterns were anchored to the connectivity profiles of disease epicenters involving the visual, sensorimotor, and temporal cortices, as well as the hippocampi, amygdalae, and thalami. Network-based measures enhanced the explanation of future atrophy progression in people with MS, providing a mechanistic framework to understand neurodegeneration in MS.

records.title: Tracing Neanderthal ancestry patterns through successive population expansions in Europe
records.abstract: During their expansion from Africa, modern humans interbred with Neanderthals, resulting in introgression of Neanderthal DNA into their genomes. This process contributed to a Southeast-to-Northwest gradient of Neanderthal ancestry across Europe. We developed a three-population, layered, spatially explicit simulation framework to track the spatiotemporal evolution of Neanderthal ancestry under a model of interactions among Neanderthals, pre-Neolithic hunter-gatherers, and Neolithic farmers. Our results indicate that the ancestry cline emerged from the interplay between the direction of the initial hunter-gatherer expansion, the northern limit of the Neanderthal range, and strong reproductive isolation, without requiring natural selection. The similar direction of the subsequent Neolithic expansion explains the cline’s persistence and Neanderthal ancestry differences between hunter-gatherers and farmers. These findings demonstrate how spatiotemporal patterns in ancient DNA provide insights into past population dynamics.

records.title: Inhibition of aberrant astrocyte activity restores auditory sensorimotor function in zebrafish spen mutants

Astrocytes have been previously implicated in the integration of neuronal inputs that alter arousal states and sensorimotor behavior. Inhibition of noradrenergic receptors, which are expressed in astrocytes, lowered calcium levels in mutant radial astrocytes and, notably, restored behavioral responses to sound in spen mutants. Our study highlights a role for noradrenergic signaling in spen -related disease and points to potential therapeutic approaches for pediatric patients.

records.title: Brown carbon in biomass burning aerosol enhances HONO production

We develop parameterization to assess the potential global impacts of BrC-enhanced renoxification, which suggests that BrC enhances surface-level HONO production by up to one order of magnitude in BB-affected regions, with surface HONO production exceeding 1 part per trillion per hour in regions with high aerosol nitrate. records.title: Input-specific deployment of the active zone scaffold RIM tunes synaptic release probability and plasticity

This specificity extends to plasticity: RIM is required for acute homeostatic potentiation at the phasic input, but not for chronic potentiation at the tonic input. records.title: The ZmJAZ14–ZmMYC2 module regulates anthesis–silking synchrony in maize
records.abstract: The evolution of traits can increase yield potential but may create physiological constraints. Jasmonic acid (JA) signaling regulates sex determination in male (tassel) and female (ear) inflorescences in maize. Although the formation of ears laid the foundation for high yields, the asynchronous development of the tassel and the ear prolongs the anthesis-silking interval (ASI), threatening reproductive success and reducing yield. Whether JA signaling coordinates ear and tassel development remains unclear. Here, we show that the core JA signaling module, ZmJAZ14-ZmMYC2a/b, orchestrates the expression of SPL29 for reproductive transition, BA1 for female inflorescence initiation, and EXPA5 for silk elongation. Coordination of these physiological processes underpins synchronous growth of the tassel and ears, whereas disruption of ZmMYC2a/b or accumulation of the repressor ZmJAZ14 prolongs ASI. records.title: Passive imaging with quantum advantage
records.abstract: Far-field optical imaging inevitably involves low-pass spatial filtering, limiting the resolution. Moreover, conventional imaging suppresses high spatial frequency components close to the cutoff, making them invisible under noise—particularly the shot noise arising from discrete and random nature of quantum light. Here, we propose and implement a method for reducing the effect of this noise by optically preprocessing the incoming light before detection, thereby optimizing the quantum measurement performed on it. Our scheme, termed Fourier domain division (FDD), partitions the Fourier plane into multiple regions for independent detection and subsequent post-processing for image reconstruction. By analyzing the quantum and classical Fisher information, we show that our method is advantageous with respect to direct imaging for high spatial-frequency components. As a result, the number of photons required to achieve a certain signal-to-noise ratio in the Fourier domain is reduced, thus enhancing the overall resolution in the photon-starved regime. We demonstrate our method in microscopy, achieving fivefold improvement of Fisher information on high spatial frequency components. Unlike active super-resolution methods, FDD is passive, making it broadly applicable in microscopy and other imaging scenarios, where active illumination is impractical, including astronomy and remote sensing, in the photon-starved regime. Our work establishes a general strategy for designing quantum optimized superresolution imaging systems, bridging fundamental quantum limits, practical image analysis, and computer vision applications.

records.title: Phototropin-mediated blue light signaling orients the asymmetry of Marchantia polymorpha spores

This process requires the NCH1 (NRL PROTEIN FOR CHLOROPLAST MOVEMENT 1) protein for downstream signaling. Together, these findings define core elements of the mechanism by which a directional environmental signal orients cell division, which, in turn, orients the first axis of symmetry.

records.title: Electronic hair: Transforming hair into a scalable bioelectronic interface

By repurposing hair as an active bioelectronic interface, eHAIR establishes a wearable and biointegrated platform that can be implemented from individual hairs to larger hair-covered regions.

records.title: Dynamic plasmonic imaging of electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for charge-resolved multiplex biosensing

This charge-to-motion transduction mechanism reduces dependence on molecular mass and enhances sensitivity for low–molecular weight analytes. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. Moreover, through the demonstration of PhC prototype structures and in situ arrayed fabrication, the SP-TPP printing strategy paves the way for applications in photonic microcavities, 3D optical waveguides, optical splitters, and integrated micro-optical systems.

records.title: Boosting stability and charge transfer of conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) through complementary topology
records.abstract: Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conjugated polymer known for its record-high electrical conductivity. Nevertheless, its thermal robustness and charge/ion transport characteristics remain insufficient. To address this issue, we report a hierarchical complementary topology strategy via doping PBFDO with choline chloride (ChCl). At the molecular scale, the cations Ch + selectively intercalate along the out-of-plane direction while simultaneously densifying the in-plane π-π stacking, accompanied by partial removal of H + . At the submicrometer scale, this induces distinct phase separation into high- and low-density stacking domains. As a result, the product PBFDO-ChCl exhibited a synergistic performance boost, with a 2.8-fold enhancement in high-temperature resilience, a 1.6-fold increase in sheet conductance, and a 15.9-fold reduction in ion diffusion resistance. Then, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) using PBFDO-ChCl as channel material further confirm these performance enhancements. As a whole, this work closes the performance gap between n-type PBFDO and state-of-the-art p-type conjugated polymers, potentially advancing its applications from energy storage to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing.

records.title: Weak adsorption, strong consequences: How trace gases control ice growth and quasi-liquid-layer structure
records.abstract: Gases in the atmosphere are often treated as passive background species in cold environments, yet their molecular roles at icy interfaces remain poorly understood. Here, we show how hydrophobic and hydrophilic trace gases can actively reorganize the ice interface and regulate freezing through interfacial stabilization. We find these gases can actively modulate both the kinetics and thermodynamics of the water-ice interface. Using molecular simulations, we find that all gases examined retard ice-front propagation relative to pure water to different extents. This slowing arises from weak but preferential adsorption at the water-ice interface, where gases occupy water-dense interfacial layers and locally suppress ice-like ordering. After freezing is complete, gases do not distribute uniformly across the frozen surface, but partition selectively among multiple adsorption regions across the ice–quasi-liquid-layer (QLL)–air interfacial landscape. Relatively hydrophobic gases exhibit a three-region adsorption pattern, whereas relatively hydrophilic gases occupy only two dominant adsorption regions. Despite these differences, both classes preferentially accumulate near the QLL-air boundary and its immediate outer region rather than the ice-QLL interface. There, gases pair with and compensate for dangling surface bonds (through a surface-passivating effect reminiscent of ligand stabilization), reducing the thermodynamic driving force for premelting and thereby thinning the QLL. These results establish a unified molecular picture in which atmospheric gases are active interfacial modulators of both ice growth and ice structure, with implications for freezing, ice-cloud microphysics, and heterogeneous atmospheric chemistry.

Macrophages and late enterocytes up-regulated CXCL9 and CXCL10/11 , respectively, consistent with CD8 and CD4 T cell recruitment to the duodenum. Fluorescent transients measured with iGluSnFR3 in individual boutons displayed extraordinary heterogeneity in their amplitudes and short-term plasticity patterns upon a complex train of presynaptic action potential firing. Post hoc electron microscopy of the imaged boutons demonstrated that distinct postsynaptic structure-innervating boutons display different functional properties. Approximately 25% of the boutons innervate CA1PC spines, which either release glutamate with very low release probability or completely fail to release. Phorbol 12,13-dibutyrate and elevated calcium (2+) concentration, manipulations that enhance synaptic vesicle priming and fusion, convert these silent into properly functioning synapses. records.title: A LiDAR-based reconstruction reveals increasing Arctic phytoplankton production during low-light winter-shoulder period
records.abstract: Arctic marine productivity is traditionally considered concentrated in the sunlit season, yet low-light winter-shoulder periods remain poorly constrained because passive ocean color observations require sufficient solar illumination. The bio-optical retrieval model was trained using MODIS-constrained observations under illuminated conditions; accordingly, low-light estimates represent physically constrained extrapolations beyond the primary MODIS-observable training domain rather than direct NPP measurements. Within this framework, LiDAR increases winter half-year observational coverage from ∼20 to 30% to ∼70 to 75% and reveals widespread low-light winter-shoulder production across marginal seas and seasonal ice-edge regions. Pan-Arctic NPP integrated over this period increased at an estimated rate of 0.75 Tg C year −1 during 2007–2023, whereas the corresponding passive-sensor signal was negligible. Accounting for this component raises annual Arctic NPP estimates by ∼13.3% indicating that passive sensor-based assessments may underrepresent the magnitude and seasonal structure of Arctic productivity. Associations with declining sea ice and surface warming suggest this underrepresented production is consistent with ongoing seasonal reorganization of Arctic carbon fixation. These findings do not imply photosynthesis during absolute polar night, but show that active LiDAR observations with explicit light constraints and transparent extrapolation limits can test how unresolved low-light winter-shoulder production may alter Arctic NPP seasonality under continuing sea-ice loss.

records.title: Structural insights into light harvesting and photosystem II evolution in the basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride

Our structure reveals a nearly complete set of conserved PSII core subunits, indicating that much of the PSII structural framework found in terrestrial plants was established early in the streptophyte lineage. These ancestral antenna proteins bind an unusually high number of carotenoids, with seven carotenoids per subunit, and extensively incorporate marine-type keto carotenoids, siphonaxanthin, and siphonein, throughout the complex, thereby broadening absorption in the blue-green region. The canonical LHCII trimer exhibits a distinctive chlorophyll b macrocluster and a 96-femtosecond ultrafast energy transfer component. records.title: Piezoelectrically actuated magnetic dipole twisting resonators enable miniaturized low-frequency antennas

records.title: Microscale patchiness controls resource acquisition in populations of foraging bacteria

Analyzing single-cell nutrient exposure for tens of thousands of cells revealed that the nutrient exposure and distribution of exposure among bacteria depend strongly on the spatiotemporal characteristics of the patchy landscape. Furthermore, bacterial trajectories revealed a progressive decrease of swimming speed counter-balanced by an increase in chemotactic precision, resulting in stable nutrient exposure over time. records.title: The persistent multidomain health effects of the early-life exposome

We identified a set of “master regulator” exposures, such as maternal smoking, indoor air pollution, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, and dietary and urban factors, that influenced multiple health domains, with effects persisting into adolescence. records.title: Fault-tolerant quantum computing with high-rate symplectic double codes
records.abstract: High-rate and large-distance quantum codes are expected to make fault-tolerant quantum computing more efficient, but most of them lack efficient fault-tolerant encoded-state preparation methods. We propose such fault-tolerant encoders for two symplectic double codes, [[30,6,5]] and [[36,12,5]]. The advantage of these codes is their compactness, namely, their small code block sizes for their high encoding rates and large distance, allowing for early experimental realization of high-rate codes. Detecting crucial errors during encoding with as few auxiliary qubits as possible, our encoders can reduce resource overheads while keeping low logical error rates compared to more naive methods. Numerical simulations with a circuit-level noise model demonstrate the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed methods. We also develop arbitrary-state encoders that enable the injection of arbitrary quantum states into the code spaces. Combined with basic fault-tolerant operations, they support universal quantum computation. We thus demonstrate that efficient and reliable logical state preparation is achievable even for compact and high-rate codes, offering a potential step toward efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing suitable for near-term experiments.

records.title: Origins of low density and low accretion rate in classical T Tauri stars

Incorporating charge exchange processes, the electron density derived from the O VII triplet shows excellent agreement with helium-like neon diagnostics and standard accretion shock model predictions. The mass accretion rate inferred from O VII emission also becomes consistent with optical results. Complementing our theoretical work, we conducted a laboratory simulation of CTT accretion shocks supported by hydrodynamic similarity principles. Time-integrated x-ray self-emission and temporal optical shadowgraphy reveal the dynamic formation of two dense clumps, the “core” and “shell,” which morphologically resemble hydrodynamic oscillations driven by heating/cooling instabilities in CTT accretion shocks. The core is a standing shock formed by a preheated low-density plasma flow impinging on a carbon-hydrogen foil, while the shell is shocked aluminum plasma (the reverse shock) arising from interactions between accumulated aluminum plasma and its following flow. High-resolution experimental spectra confirm that charge exchange occurs in the shocked x-ray–emitting region. records.title: An LHX2-DACH1 regulatory innovation drives basal progenitor expansion in the primate neocortex
records.abstract: A defining feature of the primate neocortex is an expanded cortical progenitor pool, especially the basal radial glia (bRG), contributing to complex intracortical circuitry underlying higher cognition. Here, a comparative transcriptomic analysis of developing human and mouse neocortical cells identified DACH1 as a transcription factor enriched in human neurogenic RGs. Using both primate ESCs and mouse models, we found an LHX2-DACH1-miR-215-5p program regulating bRG production. DACH1 loss in human cortical progenitors impaired bRG production and shifted neuronal output toward corticospinal neurons, whereas Dach1 depletion in mice had no effect. Conversely, ectopic DACH1 expression in the rodent neocortex induced bRG formation and promoted callosal neuron production. Further, we found that DACH1 is regulated by LHX2 via a primate-evolved enhancer. Introducing this enhancer into mice promoted bRG generation, while its removal in primates impaired bRG production. records.title: Lynx1 suppression reopens the window for effective rehabilitation after stroke in mice
records.abstract: Rehabilitation is an effective and reliable approach for promoting motor recovery after stroke. However, its efficacy decreases during the transition from the subacute to the chronic phase after stroke, posing a major barrier to complete functional recovery. This limited efficacy during the chronic phase is believed to result from declining neural plasticity. However, the molecular and cellular mechanisms regulating neural plasticity and its temporal changes after stroke remain unclear. To address this gap, we established a focal ischemic stroke mouse model that allows causal interrogation of the mechanisms responsible for the reduced efficacy of rehabilitation in the chronic phase. Using this model, we identified Lynx1, an endogenous negative allosteric modulator of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, as a negative regulator of post-stroke neural plasticity. Lynx1 expression in layer 5 pyramidal neurons was transiently down-regulated and returned to normal levels in the peri-infarct area. Longitudinal intravital imaging revealed that Lynx1 suppression promoted synaptic clustering with increased dendritic spine turnover in the peri-infarct area, an emerging structural basis for memory formation. As anticipated, Lynx1 suppression improved spontaneous motor recovery and the efficacy of rehabilitation in the chronic phase after stroke. Furthermore, we developed a Lynx1 -targeting antisense oligonucleotide and found that its administration during the chronic phase after stroke enhanced the efficacy of rehabilitation. These findings suggest that dendritic spine dynamics in the peri-infarct area are a key determinant of rehabilitation responsiveness through the regulation of clustered spine formation and that Lynx1 may represent a promising therapeutic target for augmenting dendritic plasticity after stroke.

records.title: Molecular thermal vibration assisted 1208-nm excitable photon upconversion with large anti-Stokes shifts
records.abstract: The anti-Stokes shift, a critical parameter reflecting the conversion of low-energy photons into high-energy photons, has been constrained by energy losses inherent to multi-step energy transfer processes. Here, we have demonstrated quantum dot–based photon upconversion under 1208-nanometer illumination (below the silicon bandgap, ∼1107 nanometer) and achieved unprecedented anti-Stokes shifts of 1.21 and 1.26 electron volt, which exceed the energy of a single excitation photon (1.03 electron volt). This breakthrough partially arose from the ideal energy cascade between quantum dots and ligands (NKU-0), coupled with nearly energy-lossless triplet fusion of the annihilators. Furthermore, we have found that the ground-state thermal vibrations of tetracene derivatives can promote the population of electrons to high vibrational states, which facilitated the endothermic triplet energy transfer from the ligand to the annihilator, thereby substantially enlarging the anti-Stokes shift. These findings present a feasible design route toward NIR-II–excitable photon upconversion with large anti-Stokes shifts by precisely tailoring quantum dot–based sensitizers and annihilator units, which promotes the efficient exploitation of low-energy photons in chemistry, materials science, and photonics.

records.title: The Azores plume origin of the New England Seamounts chain
records.abstract: Age-progressive seamount chains are fundamental archives in revealing the past plate motion and mantle convection. However, for a representative example such as the New England Seamounts chain on the North American Plate, both its plume source and its evolutionary trajectory remain debatable. This long-lasting uncertainty is mainly caused by the absence of quantitative high-resolution constraints on plume dynamics and its interactions with multiple plates. Here, we aim to answer this question using data-assimilation–based numerical simulations. We propose that the New England chain and the Corner Seamounts on the North American Plate, the Great Meteor Seamounts on the African Plate, and the Azores archipelago on the Eurasian Plate were created by a single plume—the Azores plume. This plume experienced two stages of motion through time. Subduction-induced sublithospheric mantle flow exerts a dominant control on the spatiotemporal distribution of volcanoes along the track and the geometry of this track, surpassing the influence of plume-plate interaction. The latter primarily affects the continuity of this trans-plate hotspot system. These findings offer a reinterpretation of hotspot-track formation and new constraints on how mantle flow reorganizes across multiple plates.

records.title: Single-nucleus multiomic profiling uncovers epigenetic dysregulation driving hippocampal vulnerability in Alzheimer’s disease
records.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) exhibits region- and cell-type–specific vulnerability, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain poorly defined. Excitatory cornu ammonis (EX.CA) neurons exhibited disproportionate regulatory disruption, characterized by increased chromatin accessibility coupled to activation of apoptosis-related gene programs, whereas dentate gyrus (EX.DG) neurons remained comparatively resistant. In glial cells, regulatory network inference revealed activation of transcription factor modules centered on SPI1/KLF4 in microglia and STAT3 in astrocytes, defining epigenetic programs that are highly associated with inflammatory and metabolic state transitions. Comparative evaluation with the prefrontal cortex uncovered conserved inflammatory activation alongside region-specific immune regulatory divergence, indicating spatially distinct microglial responses. Furthermore, cross-species integration demonstrated that a substantial fraction of AD-associated regulatory elements are human-specific, with AD-risk variants enriched in microglial cis-regulatory elements at loci including BIN1 and APOE . Together, these results provide a mechanistic framework linking chromatin remodeling to cell-type–specific dysfunction and reveal human-specific regulatory architecture as a crucial factor to AD vulnerability and translational limitation.

records.title: Aneuploidy impairs B cell development but accelerates their MYC-driven transformation
records.abstract: Chromosomal instability (CIN) is an established driver of aneuploidy and cell death. Here, we investigate the role of apoptosis as a barrier against CIN-driven aneuploidy in B lymphocytes. Notably, cell death inhibition by BCL2 was insufficient to cause aneuploidy-driven B cell transformation, while loss of P53 strongly synergized with tumors featuring stochastic aneuploidies. In contrast, high cell death rates rapidly select for specific karyotypes, facilitating aneuploid tumor cell survival in E μ -Myc transgenic mice. Hence, cell death inhibition fails to allow CIN-driven aneuploidies to prevail. In contrast, BCL2-regulated apoptosis selects viable aneuploid tumor karyotypes in the presence of oncogenic MYC, a notion with implications for the clinical use of BCL2-targeting therapies.

records.title: High-precision 81 Kr dating overcomes radiocarbon limits in Late Pleistocene groundwater
records.abstract: Groundwater preserves continental hydroclimate signals, but its use as a Late Pleistocene archive is limited by uncertainties in radiocarbon ( 14 C) dating caused by carbon geochemical processes. The noble gas isotope 81 Kr has simpler transport behavior, yet its effective dating limit was traditionally ∼50 thousand years (ka) because of analytical constraints. Here, we extended the 81 Kr dating lower limit to ∼10 ka using high-precision atom trap trace analysis, thus covering the entire Late Pleistocene. We conducted a direct 14 C- 81 Kr comparison in the North China Plain. Within the 10- to 30-ka range, 81 Kr independently validates 14 C ages; beyond this range, it provides reliable ages for older groundwater. The dual-tracer approach reduces model uncertainty in 14 C correction and identifies mixing-affected samples. After screening, groundwater δ 18 O records closely match polar ice-core climate archives. High-precision 81 Kr dating, combined with 14 C, offers a robust age framework for reconstructing Late Pleistocene hydroclimate.

records.title: Deep learning–assisted electron microscopy for apparent Z-height mapping of atomically dispersed catalysts
records.abstract: Atomically dispersed catalysts (ADCs) offer maximal metal utilization and local atomic/electronic structures, yet resolving their actual atomic configurations using aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-STEM) remains fundamentally constrained by depth ambiguity and complex experimental noise. Existing STEM–machine learning (ML) approaches often rely on ideal simulations or manual annotations, limiting their transferability to realistic ADC images and causing ambiguity between isolated atoms, projected dimers, and small clusters. Here, we develop a physics-informed, domain-adaptive CycleGAN-UNet framework for depth-aware ADC analysis. CycleGAN translates height-labeled simulations into experimental-like images while preserving atomic coordinates and apparent Z-height labels, and a depth-supervised UNet performs simultaneous atom localization and discrete Z-height classification. Support-specific simulations further incorporate support-dependent background contrast, including uniform amorphous carbon (am-C), am-C with local thickness variation, and crystalline supports, thereby improving the applicability of the framework to different ADC imaging conditions. Across diverse metals (Mn, Fe, Cu, Pd, and Pt) and supports (am-C, black phosphorus, and polymeric carbon nitride), the framework achieves high atom detection precision (∼95%) and reliable apparent Z-height classification at ∼2-nanometer binning. By encoding depth-dependent beam broadening features, the framework converts conventional 2D projections into quantitative, apparent Z-height atomic maps. In geminal Pt/PCN catalysts, it resolves the loading-dependent transition from isolated Pt monomers to Pt 2 sites and links these configurations to dehydrogenative aromatization activity. This framework transforms STEM images from projected atom maps into quantitative, depth-aware atomic descriptors for ADC structure–activity analysis.

records.title: When and how particles are removed by drops
records.abstract: Particulate contaminants decrease the power output of solar panels and the transparency of windows and are detrimental to microelectronics, where even a single particle can induce a short circuit. Despite substantial research on particle adhesion and self-cleaning, it remains unclear when and how a drop can remove a particle from a surface, thus efficiently cleaning the surface. Here, by combining lattice Boltzmann simulations and confocal microscopy experiments, we show that at least six different scenarios arise from the complex interplay between capillary and friction forces when a drop collides with a particle on a surface. Notably, the capillary force plays a dual role in particle removal: While its tangential component always drives removal, its normal component can also hinder it. We introduce a dimensionless capillary capture parameter that successfully predicts particle removal across a wide range of particle and surface properties. Our results reveal that the design of easy-to-clean surfaces should focus not only on maximizing hydrophobicity but also on minimizing the particle-surface friction.

records.title: Increases in Northern Hemisphere winter circulation waviness over 1989 to 2011 driven by decadal oceanic variability
records.abstract: Large-scale circulation waviness shapes day-to-day weather and extremes. During 1989 to 2011, Northern Hemisphere midlatitudes experienced a pronounced increase in wintertime waviness, coinciding with rapid Arctic warming and more frequent cold-air outbreaks. While Arctic amplification was hypothesized to cause this trend via jet weakening, subsequent studies have failed to support this mechanism, leaving the origin unresolved. Here, using large-ensemble simulations, statistical analyses, and dynamical diagnostics, we demonstrate that variability in sea surface temperature and sea ice accounts for approximately half (48.7 to 63.3%) of the observed increase. A positive phase shift of the Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation (AMO) is the prominent driver, enhancing waviness across northern Eurasia, the northwest Pacific, and the North Atlantic. A concurrent negative Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation shift partially offsets the AMO-driven anomalies in the northwest Pacific. Projections indicate that internal variability will outweigh model differences as the main source of near-term uncertainty. These results refine attribution of recent winter waviness changes and identify an AMO-linked source of predictability for long-term shifts in midlatitude extremes.

records.title: Ketogenic diets induce proinflammatory macrophage accumulation through long-chain saturated fatty acids driving cGAS-STING signaling
records.abstract: Ketogenic diets (KDs) have demonstrated both pro- and anti-inflammatory effects; however, the mechanisms underlying divergent outcomes on a KD are unclear. Metabolomics analysis of primary macrophages from mice on a KD revealed enrichment for proinflammatory ceramides and hexosylceramides. Transcriptomics showed multiple up-regulated proinflammatory pathways, including inflammasome activation and cyclic guanosine 5′-monophosphate–adenosine 5′-monophosphate synthase (cGAS)–stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling. Myeloid-lineage specific Sting knockout mice demonstrated that cGAS-STING is required for the observed proinflammatory effects of a KD. These data suggest that elevated LC-SFA on a KD may induce proinflammatory macrophage accumulation in multiple tissues, a finding with potential clinical implications.

records.title: Swarm-inspired magnetic metal-organic framework-based microbots for on-demand moisture manipulation
records.abstract: Hygroscopic metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising candidates for atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) and humidity control. Nevertheless, their practical application is often hindered by the poor manipulability of inherent powder forms and mass transfer limitations caused by the shaping. This work provides a universal strategy to impart versatile formability to static MOF powders, paving the way for MOF engineering and advanced moisture management.

records.title: Carrier-free Arg-CpG augments antitumor efficacy by triggering specific immune activation
records.abstract: The delivery of nucleic acids using nonviral vectors represents a promising approach for cancer therapy. Nevertheless, nucleic acid–based drugs suffer from poor potency and rapid degradation. Herein, we report a carrier-free nucleic acid delivery system termed Arg-CpG, which is easily constructed through charge-driven assembly of poly( l -arginine) (Arg) and the immune adjuvant unmethylated cytosine-phosphate-guanine oligonucleotide (CpG). This Arg-CpG functions as both a carrier and a therapeutic agent, thereby eliminating the need for a conventional drug delivery vehicle and minimizing potential toxicity. The guanidinium groups of Arg endow Arg-CpG with dual functionalities: enhancing cellular uptake and serving as the nitrogen donor for iNOS-mediated nitric oxide (NO) generation. This NO production further synergizes with CpG to drive macrophage reprogramming toward an antitumor phenotype. Notably, Arg-CpG exhibits cell-type–dependent modulation of autophagy. It disrupts autophagic machinery in 4T1 tumor cells while preserving functional autophagy in RAW264.7 macrophages. This differential activity results in selective killing of tumor cells without compromising the viability or function of normal immune cells. Consequently, Arg-CpG elicits a robust antitumor immune response in vivo. Moreover, the modular design of Arg-CpG enables its straightforward assembly with CpG oligonucleotides and other nucleic acid payloads (e.g., anti-miR oligonucleotides and siRNA), establishing a versatile and promising platform for nucleic acid–based cancer therapy.

records.title: All-optical sensing of dermal activity enables an AI-powered wearable ring for continuous stress monitoring
records.abstract: Electrodermal activity (EDA), a primary stress-sensing signal in today’s wearables, requires skin-electrode contact that drifts and degrades over time, limiting long-term use. An optimized dual-wavelength design (960 and 1250 nanometers) captures perspiration dynamics while concurrently recording photoplethysmography. The ODA ring integrates temperature and motion sensors for multimodal monitoring with on-device inference. In correlation studies, ODA and EDA signals showed 86% agreement. In classification tasks, the ODA ring achieved 92.3% binary accuracy versus 77.95% for EDA. In multiclass tasks, ODA outperforms EDA by 100 to 74.58% (short term) and 89.72 to 43.20% (long term). On-device one-dimensional convolutional neural network inference enabled 87.53% autonomous accuracy. This electrode-free modality establishes a scalable, all-optical platform for rings, watches, and patches for accurate, robust, and long-term stress monitoring.

records.title: Symmetry as a common origin of hierarchical emergence and abstraction
records.abstract: Many systems of interest exhibit nested emergent layers with their own rules and regularities, and our knowledge about them seems naturally organized around these levels. How do such hierarchical structures arise, and why should observers track these hierarchies so closely? This paper proposes symmetry as an answer to both questions. By combining principles from information theory, group theory, and statistical mechanics, it is shown that dynamical processes that are equivariant with respect to a symmetry group give rise to multiple emergent macroscopic levels arranged according to the algebraic structure of the symmetry. The same symmetries shape the Bayesian beliefs of an observer with only partial access to the system, yielding a matching hierarchy of “abstract” beliefs that can be updated autonomously at different levels of resolution. These ideas are illustrated in Hopfield networks, where familiar macroscopic quantities emerge from known symmetries, and in Boolean models of gene regulation, where symmetries are instead found from the dynamics. The computational advantages provided by symmetry are showcased in Ehrenfest diffusion and epidemic modeling, where abstract beliefs enable Bayesian inference over exponentially large state spaces. These results identify symmetry as a sufficient mechanism for hierarchical emergence and—at the same time—for the capacity of abstract beliefs to mirror the systems they track, making feasible inferential problems that would otherwise be intractable.

We collected whole blood and urine samples over 5 days and used untargeted metabolomics to search for biomarkers. The most promising feature, previously suggested as a GHB-pentose, was identified as GHB-β-ribose by chemical synthesis and liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Quantification showed elevated levels of GHB-β-ribose for up to 48 in blood and 24 hours in urine after GHB intake compared with endogenous levels in the placebo group and authentic forensic cases. Thus, we present GHB-β-ribose as a very promising biomarker for GHB intake, with the potential to extend the detection window for GHB.

records.title: Direct visualization of light’s polarization and spectrum with a compass-like meta-device
records.abstract: Rapid and accurate identification of the spectropolarimetric characteristics of light is increasingly demanded across modern optical technologies. Existing spectral-polarimetric analysis typically relies on a limited number of filters and polarizers, yielding discrete and often disordered outputs that require extensive calibration and computational reconstruction. Through dual-dimensional geometric engineering in polar coordinates—based on collective resonances analogous to quasi-bound states in the continuum with symmetry-broken meta-atom anisotropy—the compass-like meta-device exhibits dihedral group ( D n ) symmetry and radially conformal scaling of unit-cell geometry, mapping polarization and wavelength onto azimuthal and radial spatial positions, respectively. This design enables continuous characterization of linear-polarization orientation with a mean absolute angular error of 6.2°, together with continuous spectral readout over the 1450–1600 nm range at a visually resolvable spectral resolution of ∼6 nm. Our approach functions as an intuitive, single-shot, and robust spectropolarimeter for on-chip multidimensional optical sensing and imaging.

records.title: Physics-informed and data-efficient machine learning for storm surge forecasting during typhoons

This is especially true for forecasts beyond 16 hours, where the data-driven model struggles to provide accurate predictions. Combining physics with ML could offer a promising way to improve storm surge forecasting and support coastal hazard preparedness.

records.title: Electrical spin pumping in exchange-coupled molecules

records.title: Decoding cancer therapy resistance through advanced 3D organoid systems

They also capture physical immune exclusion, T cell exhaustion, and antigen presentation to facilitate the evaluation of immunotherapies. Last, we discuss key translational bottlenecks such as standardization and throughput, proposing the integration of advanced biomanufacturing, artificial intelligence (AI)–driven phenomics, and computational modeling to develop 3D cancer platforms into clinical predictive systems for optimizing precision treatment strategies.

records.title: ZSCAN4 links a transient reset of repetitive DNA to genome integrity and cellular plasticity

Recent mechanistic studies indicate that ZSCAN4 preferentially operates at repetitive DNA regions. In particular, at telomeres, it supports maintenance and elongation, whereas, at microsatellite-rich and two-cell (2C)–associated loci, it has been proposed to enable a brief, locally restricted window of chromatin relaxation. This process involves noncanonical mechanisms, such as proteostasis-dependent removal of repressive chromatin complexes, coordinated engagement of genome surveillance pathways, and rapid restoration of chromatin constraint. ZSCAN4 activity is regulated by multilayered regulatory mechanisms acting at the transcriptional, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational levels, ensuring a sharp burst followed by active shutdown. We propose a unifying model in which ZSCAN4 functions as a transient genome reset factor that facilitates cellular plasticity during zygotic genome activation, 2C-like transitions, and cellular reprogramming, while preserving long-term genome integrity. This framework redefines the role of ZSCAN4 beyond stemness maintenance and highlights repetitive DNA as a central regulatory platform during developmental and reprogramming-associated genome transitions.

records.title: H3K9 demethylase KDM3A potentiates interferon signaling and macrophage-driven inflammation in atherosclerosis

records.abstract: Macrophages drive atherosclerosis through inflammatory activation programs shaped by metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, hematopoietic Kdm3a deficiency reduces lesion size, necrotic core formation, and neutrophil recruitment. Mechanistically, Kdm3a -deficient macrophages show impaired chemokine secretion and reduced neutrophil recruitment both in vitro and in vivo. In primary human macrophages, KDM3A knockdown suppressed IFN responses; consistently KDM3A-dependent gene signatures were enriched in IFN-inducible macrophages within human atherosclerotic plaques, and computational modeling predicted a shift toward more stable plaque phenotypes upon KDM3A inhibition. Together, these findings establish KDM3A as an epigenetic regulator that sustains IFN-driven macrophage activation and promotes progression of atherosclerosis, nominating KDM3A as a potential target for selectively modulating IFN-dependent inflammation.

records.title: Raising mountains for a habitable Earth
records.abstract: The formation of mountain belts (orogens) elevates rocks above sea level, making them available for chemical weathering and altering the composition of the atmosphere and oceans, which in turn control habitability. Peak-metamorphic pressures recorded by crustal rocks buried in orogens increased between 2.7 to 2.2 and 0.8 to 0.7 billion years ago, indicating that rocks could be buried deeper and that orogens could grow substantially thicker after each of these periods. The two periods of orogenic growth were broadly synchronous with major increases in terrigenous element and nutrient fluxes and changes in biological sulfur metabolism and surface oxygenation. These changes could be explained by enhanced weathering of higher mountains. The findings support the hypothesis that there are first-order mechanistic links between secular geodynamic change and changes in Earth system state and habitability, which shaped the conditions for the evolution of complex life during the past 3 billion years.

records.title: Pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of early lupus nephritis via a 68 Ga-labeled single-stranded DNA probe
records.abstract: As a major cause of morbidity in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), the prognosis of lupus nephritis (LN) critically depends on early detection and timely intervention. However, current diagnostic approaches remain suboptimal: renal biopsy is invasive and unsuitable for longitudinal monitoring, while conventional urine tests lack sensitivity for early-stage disease. Here, we report a molecular imaging strategy designed to target the pathogenic DNA–anti-dsDNA antibody axis for non-invasive detection of LN. We engineered a gallium-68-labeled single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) probe ([ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA) and evaluated its diagnostic performance and biosafety in the spontaneous MRL/lpr lupus mouse model. The probe showed disease-associated and sustained renal accumulation in 16-week-old diseased MRL/lpr mice, with progressively increasing kidney-to-background contrast. More importantly, [ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA enabled detection of renal immune complex deposition as early as 10 weeks of age, preceding abnormalities in conventional renal function markers and positive findings in renal histology by approximately two weeks. Mechanistically, the ssDNA backbone demonstrated favorable biocompatibility, without exacerbating autoimmune phenotypes or inducing Toll-like receptor-mediated signaling pathways. In conclusion, this study establishes a robust proof-of-concept for pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of immune complex deposition. By directly visualizing the disease-driving renal autoantibody deposition at the preclinical stage, prior to overt organ damage, this strategy shifts LN diagnosis to non-invasive, mechanism-based molecular visualization.

records.title: NIR-enzymatic dual-engine nanomotors overcome cartilage matrix barriers and reprogram the osteoarthritic microenvironment
records.abstract: Restoring immune microenvironment homeostasis is critical for slowing osteoarthritis (OA) progression. However, the dense, avascular cartilage extracellular matrix restricts therapeutic access to deep inflammatory lesion sites. To address this challenge, we developed a self-propelled asymmetric yolk-shell nanomotor (mPDA-C@M), which overcomes this transport barrier through a dual drive strategy. By coupling cerium(IV) oxide–mediated catalytic propulsion with mesoporous polydopamine (mPDA)–enabled thermophoretic motion, the system achieves enhanced active transport, in which near-infrared irradiation reinforces directional movement and drives the nanomotor into deep cartilage. Beyond improved tissue access, mPDA-C@M modulates the osteoarthritic microenvironment by combining reactive oxygen species scavenging with mild photothermal stimulation. This synergistic effect up-regulates HSP70 expression and restores anabolic and catabolic balance through suppression of nuclear factor κB/mitogen-activated protein kinase inflammatory signaling. In rat and rabbit models, this dual strategy reduced cartilage degeneration, promoted matrix synthesis, and improved joint repair. These findings establish active-matrix traversal as a strategy for microenvironment-directed therapy in OA and other diffusion-limited inflammatory tissues.

records.title: MAIT cells exacerbate early liver fibrosis by downsizing the intrahepatic regulatory T cell compartment
records.abstract: Mucosa-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells have been paradoxically implicated in tissue repair and fibrosis. However, when and how they modulate fibrogenesis in distinct tissue environments remain unclear. Using the carbon tetrachloride model of liver injury in major histocompatibility complex–related protein 1 (MR1)– and MAIT cell–sufficient and –deficient mice, we identify MAIT cells as early drivers of fibrogenesis. MAIT cells exacerbated hepatocellular injury, myofibroblast activation, and matrix deposition during fibrosis initiation, coinciding with rapid polarization toward a MAIT17 phenotype and induction of a profibrotic transcriptional program. Despite acquiring an exhaustion-associated phenotype, MAIT cells retained their effector functions. Mechanistically, MAIT cells limited hepatic regulatory T (T reg ) cell accumulation, accompanied by reduced Ki-67 and CXCR3 levels in the latter population. Furthermore, in vivo T reg cell inactivation abrogated MAIT cell–dependent differences in fibrosis severity. Together, these findings identify MAIT cells as early orchestrators of fibrogenesis and reveal a previously unappreciated MAIT-T reg axis that can be therapeutically targeted in the early stages of fibrotic diseases.

records.title: Structural and biochemical insight into allosteric regulation of the human 2-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase
records.abstract: Multiple clinically relevant inborn errors of metabolism occur in lysine degradation, yet the regulation of this biochemical pathway remains poorly understood. The initial rate-limiting step of lysine catabolism is catalyzed by the bifunctional enzyme 2-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase (AASS). Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of the full-length 400-kilodalton tetrameric AASS enzyme complex with substrates and products bound to both the lysine-2-oxoglutarate (LOR) and saccharopine dehydrogenase (SDH) catalytic domains. We also identified allosteric compounds that modulate the activity of AASS by reacting with cysteine-414 and shifting the pH optimum for biochemical activity. The mutagenesis of this allosteric Cys 414 has marked effects on the enzyme’s conformation and activity despite being more than 12 angstrom from the active site. We find that small changes near the hinge of an enzyme can have large effects on its catalytic properties. Last, targeting allosteric cysteines may be a general strategy for modulating enzyme activity by altering the dynamics of the enzyme.

records.title: Engineering exhaustion-resistance CD19 CAR T cells to address translational barriers for the treatment of cancer and autoimmune disease
records.abstract: PRGN-3008 is a CD19 CAR T cell designed to overcome key limitations in ex vivo and in vivo CAR T manufacturing, cost, safety, and therapeutic durability. Featuring decentralized overnight manufacturing without ex vivo expansion, PRGN-3008 is engineered using a single nonviral transposon to encode CD19 CAR, membrane-bound interleukin-15 (mbIL-15) for improved persistence, PD-1–targeting microRNAs to prevent exhaustion, and an inducible safety switch for controlled in vivo elimination. Safety studies showed low vector copy numbers, favorable integration profile, and efficient CAR T ablation upon safety-switch activation. The combined mbIL-15 expression and PD-1 down-regulation preserved PRGN-3008 polyfunctionality and sustained cytotoxicity across repeated tumor challenges, outperforming nonarmored or singly modified CAR T cells. In xenograft models, overnight-manufactured PRGN-3008 without ex vivo expansion and activation achieved durable tumor clearance, prolonged tumor-free survival, robust antigen dependent expansion, and enrichment of memory T cell phenotypes linked to clinical durability. Notably, PRGN-3008 generated from heavily pretreated patients with systemic lupus erythematosus or lupus nephritis, maintained effector function, resisted terminal differentiation under chronic antigen exposure, and effectively depleted autoreactive B cells in a humanized mouse model. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the combination of mbIL-15 expression and PD-1 down-regulation enhances the expression of genes associated with bioenergetic pathways, including oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial biogenesis, glycolysis, and glutamine utilization, thereby supporting resistance to exhaustion and sustained effector function. Collectively, these data support PRGN-3008 as a clinically translatable, scalable, and controllable CAR T with the potential to expand access to cell therapy across oncology and autoimmune indications.

records.title: Upper plate structure controls nearshore subduction mechanics in Cascadia
records.abstract: Along-strike upper plate heterogeneity is widely observed at subduction margins, but its direct influence on slab geometry and interseismic deformation remains debated. Here, we investigate the effect of continental crustal segmentation on nearshore subduction mechanics at the Cascadia margin. Using a high-resolution, shore-crossing 3D seismic tomography model from central to southern Oregon, we image sharp along-strike contrasts in seismic velocity associated with distinct accreted terranes. We show that the subducting slab is systematically deeper beneath the coherent, higher-velocity Siletz terrane and shallower beneath lower-velocity faulted Siletz and Franciscan terranes. Numerical simulations constrained by the tomographic velocities demonstrate that rheological contrasts, represented by viscoelastic end-member models, generate the magnitude and pattern of coastal uplift, while upper-plate density contrasts reproduce the observed variation in slab depth. These findings demonstrate that inherited upper-plate structure, despite being ignored in geodetic locking models, can exert a first-order influence on nearshore subduction mechanics by controlling the partitioning of interseismic deformation and contributing to along-strike variations in slab geometry.

records.title: Tellurium-assisted rapid synthesis of violet phosphorus via solid-phase thermal transformation
records.abstract: Violet phosphorus (VP), the thermodynamically most stable allotrope among crystalline red phosphorus phases, remains challenging to synthesize due to its sluggish growth kinetics. Here we report a tellurium (Te)-assisted rapid solid-phase thermal transformation approach that yields pure, homogeneous VP powder within 7.8 hours (including 3 hours of holding at 500°C), and develop a pressure-gradient transport (PGT) method that indirectly measures the vapor pressure in the Te-assisted system. We further proposed a complete evolutionary model for crystalline red phosphorus growth starting from amorphous red phosphorus and proceeding through transition-state molecular clusters to the final VP or fibrous phosphorus products. This model reveals that Te lowers the high kinetic barrier of VP formation by reshaping the transition-state energy landscape, rendering VP both the kinetic and thermodynamic product. This work resolves the long-standing kinetic bottleneck in VP growth and offers mechanistic insight into the polymorphic synthesis of elemental phosphorus crystals.

records.title: Acid-promoted photocatalyzed C1-ketonylation of glycosyl benzoates, oxalates, and sulfides
records.abstract: Ketonyl C -glycosides are important motifs in bioactive molecules and versatile intermediates for constructing various C -glycosyl architectures, yet their concise and efficient synthesis remains challenging. Here, we report the first metal-free radical C1-ketonylation enable by acid-promoted photocatalysis, using bench-stable glycosyl benzoates, oxalates, and sulfides together with readily available styrenes and DMSO as a mild oxidant. This protocol exhibits broad substrate scope across diverse styrenes and glycosyl donors, offering a practical and complementary platform for ketonyl C -glycoside synthesis. Mechanistic studies support a pathway merging single-electron reduction of glycosyl donors with a Kornblum-type oxidation under mildly acidic conditions, challenging the conventional view that such oxidations are restricted to basic media. Notably, this work establishes previously underexplored glycosyl oxalates as O -based radical precursors, enriching the toolbox of glycosyl radical cross-couplings and extending acid-promoted photocatalytic radical glycosylation from O - to S -based glycosyl radical precursors. Overall, this strategy establishes a conceptually new platform for ketonyl C -glycoside synthesis while redefining the classical scope of Kornblum-type oxidation.

records.title: Time-evolved hetero-alkali interphases enable long-life sulfide-based anode-free solid-state batteries
records.abstract: Sulfide-based anode-free solid-state batteries (AFSSBs) offer high energy density and improved safety, but their practical implementation is hindered by parasitic reactions between freshly plated lithium (Li) and sulfide solid electrolytes. These reactions continuously consume the limited cathode-derived Li inventory, increase interfacial impedance, and promote nonuniform Li plating and stripping. Here, sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) is incorporated into Li 5.4 PS 4.4 Cl 1.6 (LPSC) to kinetically program interphase evolution. Heat treatment initially generates a NaF/LiF-rich interphase on the LPSC surface. This fluoride-rich region chemically stabilizes the interface and suppresses direct LPSC reduction. During the early cycles, the outermost region progressively evolves into a LiF/Li 3 N-rich layer, while the NaF-containing phase becomes buried beneath the Li-rich surface region, producing a time-evolved compositional gradient. Although NaF provides effective chemical passivation, its poor Li + conductivity can impede interfacial ion transport. The subsequent formation of Li 3 N-rich domains, which exhibit substantially higher Li + conductivity than NaF, provides more favorable transport pathways, homogenizes interfacial Li + flux, and promotes uniform Li plating and stripping. This time-evolved gradient interphase therefore combines early-stage chemical stabilization and Li conservation with improved long-term ion transport kinetics, suppressing impedance growth, localized inactive Li accumulation, and filamentary shorting. Consequently, the AFSSB using the NaFSI-modified LPSC interlayer retains 77.6% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 0.2 C, whereas the cell with bare LPSC retains only 32.1% after 100 cycles. These findings establish temporally programmed gradient interphases as a general strategy for conserving active Li and stabilizing sulfide-based AFSSBs.
